speaker: The Chairman
text: Head X, Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We know that views on issues of social importance are progressively becoming more diverse across a wider spectrum of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Our youths, who form the bedrock of our future, are decidedly more seized with such issues and are inclined to speak their minds, even on sensitive issues of race and religion.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: The proliferation of inter-racial and intercultural marriages in Singapore will lead to a new generation of Singaporeans that will hold a fresh perspective on racial and cultural identity.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: An ageing population will require us to review our national policies to address the issues arising, but also to consider how Singaporean families fundamentally function as a foundational unit that is entrusted with bringing up the next generation and caring for our seniors.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We must never take for granted the social harmony that was painstakingly built over successive generations of Singaporeans since our Independence.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Having said that, I remain optimistic, that discourse that is constructive and respectful can allow us to better reflect upon how we could refresh our social compact and strengthen our sense of national unity and identity.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: As we have shown to have done in our history, we can harness diversity as an agent for unity, rather than divisiveness.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We must therefore think of how we can contribute to the larger society.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The Malay/Muslim community, like any other group in Singapore, does not exist in isolation.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have some suggestions on how the Malay/Muslim community can expand its contributions to the nation as it does better for itself.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Second, the sharing of cultural heritage should not be limited to Racial Harmony Day and major festivals.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Post-COVID-19, I look forward to the resumption of mosque open houses and other events at which Singaporeans can gain an understanding of our diverse cultural fabric.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We should also learn from the best practices of Muslim minority communities in other countries.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How can we encourage individuals, organisations and our religious institutions to step forward, and play their part in fostering social harmony and in building a better Singapore?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How can we share stories of successful Singaporean Malay/Muslims abroad even more?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They carry our Singapore flag in other countries in various fields.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can we scour more globally those that have ventured abroad and have contributed to Singapore's Gross national product versus Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: (In Malay):   Statistics from 2010 to 2020 show that our Malay Singaporeans are able to secure better jobs and give their families a better standard of life today.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Just like how the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic had disrupted lives and livelihoods, our exit from the pandemic will similarly bring about new economic uncertainties and challenges.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: China has just reopened its economy to the world earlier this year.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Increased geopolitical tensions have worsened the uncertain outlook.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In the same way that the Government and self-help organisations such as the AMP had supported the Malay/Muslim community throughout the pandemic, in the form of skills upgrading and re-skilling opportunities, I am sure our Mala/Muslim professionals will not be left to navigate today’s uncertain waters alone.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What are the plans to better support our Malay/Muslim professionals to ensure that they remain employable and can progress in their chosen careers?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First, as the world has re-opened, we should encourage our Malay/Muslim professionals and workers to be adaptable and experience new challenges.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Perhaps the Ministry can look into the statistics of, and opportunities for, our Malay/Muslim professionals to go abroad for overseas secondments and training opportunities.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can we form partnerships with a few Temasek-linked companies to meet specific targets?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Second, perhaps we can think about how to further utilise the SkillsFuture Credit scheme between 2015 and 2020.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: (In Malay):   Who is the Malay Singaporean and what are his contributions to the nation?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: The truth is, the Malay community is a diverse community, with many talents.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: The Malay Singaporean is a CIO at the IMF.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: The Malay Singaporean is Singapore's favourite footballing son.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: The Malay Singaporean is a top trade negotiator.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: The Malay Singaporean is a navy officer, an army officer, a police officer, an SCDF officer, a healthcare worker.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: The Malay Singaporean is the champion of the side hustle, from gifted photographers to thriving home based business that bring joy to customers.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: In an increasingly noisy and uncertain world, by practicing the values of our culture including humility, respect, moral and ethical living and family, we can continue to set an example.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: How do we best harness the talents of the Malay community and inspire and motivate ourselves to build a community of success, and to be recognized for our contributions to the nation?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: (In Malay):   Mr Chairman, I would like to seek clarification as well as share a suggestion on some matters related to the Malay-Muslim community.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The first is about the Community Leaders Forum (CLF).

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: First, what is the status of the CLF?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Second, is the function of CLF still relevant after the establishment of M3?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Third, what is the difference between these two platforms and whether, there is duplication between them?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Chairman, is about the Malay-Muslim Community Development Fund or MMCDF which was established in 1991 to assist Malay/Muslim organisations in their efforts to empower the community.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Next, I would like to touch on efforts to help the Muslim community understand, embrace and deal with Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual and Transgender (LGBT) issues in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: At the beginning of 2022, PERGAS formed a special task force team for LGBT issues.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Among the efforts held by PERGAS are dialogue sessions with Muslim individuals from the LGBT community and also provide guidance to the Muslim community in Singapore on facing and managing this issue.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: As I said in my Committee of Supply speech last year, I welcome PERGAS's initiative.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Mr Chairman, in November last year, this House passed an amendment bill to repeal section 377A.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The fourth and last point is about the efforts on the part of the Minister and the ruling party Malay/Muslim MPs regarding the use of tudung for uniformed groups in the public service.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Mr Chairman, there have been several times when the tudung issue was raised in this House, the Minister in-charge of Muslim Affairs, either the current or the previous one, has said that such matters should be discussed in a closed session or behind closed doors.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The last time this was said was two years ago during the 2021 Committee of Supply debates when it was recommended that nurses in the public health sector be given permission to don the tudung.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: If there is, how many sessions have been held and, if no, why?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Malay)   Sir, Malay/Muslim organisations (MMOs) play a vital role in providing support for the community and are valuable Government partners.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Veteran MMO leaders have contributed a lot to the community's development.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, to ensure MMOs' continued relevance and success, leadership renewal must become a key focus area for any organisation.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This programme was established to nurture the next generation of MMO leaders, equipping them with the knowledge, skills and networks to lead the Malay/Muslim community and their organizations.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How can the Government support the MMOs' planning so that their efforts and programmes continue to be relevant for this generation and the next?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How can MMOs play a greater role in nation and community building, and are there plans to support synergised efforts among MMOs as well as encourage collaboration with non-MMOs?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Chairman, a strong and resilient family is a cornerstone in the development of highly confident individuals and children, and a successful society.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Apart from the efforts and initiatives at the national level to help various groups in our community, including strengthening families and marriages, programs carried out by M3 also complement the efforts within the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As the former chairman of M3@Towns, I have witnessed the development and approaches of M3 which are now more extensive and has a greater impact on the families within our community who participated in M3 programs and initiatives.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Presently, each M3@ Town has its own characteristic and creates programs customized to the town's demographics.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This was evident during the exhibition and sharing session at the recent M3 Forum.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For example the initiatives at M3@Chua Chu Kang, are based on a strategy to build current and future leaders of families.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This strategy is called Nakhoda Bahtera (Captain of the Ship), in which family leaders steers the future of their families in navigating the ocean of life containing waves of challenges.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, in order to build strong family leaders and resilient families, we need all hands on deck.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Can the Minister share the initiatives that can enable our partners and community organisations to better support married couples in building strong marriages and families?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Dr Shahira Abdullah, please take your three cuts together.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: (In Malay)   The Bersamamu Programme is a great initiative by the Naib Kadis that aims to guide and support a newlywed couple for the first two years of marriage.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: While the program has been successful in providing much-needed guidance and assistance to couples, I believe that there is a need for a female perspective to be included in the program.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: (In Malay):   Wakaf Masyarakat is a noble initiative which is a form of endowment that is dedicated to social and community projects.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Another concern is whether the establishment of Wakaf Masyarakat will increase competition and create donation fatigue or affect donation streams for other social service MMOs.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: It is imperative to strike a balance to ensure that other social service MMOs are not adversely affected.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: (In Malay):   As asatizahs shift to secular careers, can I ask the Ministry how we can encourage their continued contribution to the religious development of the community?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: This group can have regular meetings, conferences, or other events that bring them together and enable them to share their knowledge and experiences.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: It can provide mentorship opportunities and help asatizahs stay engaged with the community and give back through their knowledge and expertise.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Asatizahs who have shifted to secular careers may be interested in mentoring younger members of the community who are pursuing religious education or careers.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: The network can also provide opportunities for asatizahs who have shifted to secular careers to teach or lead Islamic programs on a part time basis.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: (In Malay)   History has taught us how many Muslim minority communities all over the world are not only able to adapt in non-Muslim countries but also enjoy success that makes their country proud and benefits its plural society in general.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: In fact, there is a specific jurisprudence in Islam to deal with the contemporary realities experienced by Muslim minority communities.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Muslim minority communities in countries like Singapore face many unique challenges that differ from the Muslim majority communities.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Now with many ideologies that are more divisive, the challenges we face are becoming more critical and it is important that we address these issues together with all Muslim minority communities globally.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Thus, the International Conference on Communities of Success (ICCOS) held last year aims to enable sharing within a scientific framework for Muslim minority communities when facing the challenges of today.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Dr Wan Rizal, please take your two cuts together.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: (In Malay)   Singapore is a multicultural and multireligious country, where people of different ethnicities and faith can coexist peacefully.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Our asatizahs play a significant role in the Muslim community.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: They are a key pillar who serve as guides to enable Malay/Muslims to practice our faith confidently while being integral members of the larger Singapore nation.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: They provide contextualised religious guidance for our community and offer sound religious advice on contemporary issues.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: This was evident during the COVID-19 pandemic, where they navigated and rallied our community with calmness and compassion.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: They provided much-needed support and guidance during an extremely challenging time.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: However, I believe, beyond the pandemic, our asatizah have the potential to significantly impact society as a whole.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We have seen how the many mosques in Singapore, driven by our asatizah, work closely with the community at large.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Recently, asatizah from the mosque has collaborated with Geylang Market Traders Association and Wisma Geylang to organize public motivational talks related to mental health.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Could the Minister share how our asatizah can make more meaningful contributions beyond the Muslim community to benefit the larger Singapore society?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: (In Malay)   Sir, some segments of our community still need more assistance than others.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: One particular group is those who live in public rental flats.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: At M3@Jalan Besar, I have seen the positive impact of well-organised and highly synergised efforts from the volunteers and the multi-agency task force.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I am encouraged when residents shared that they are getting support in terms of employment advice, children's education and they are working towards owning their own flats.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I hope we can do more, but I also understand its challenges.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We may need to recruit more volunteers and at the same time ensure that inter-agency task force is not stretched until its operations on the ground becomes affected.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Mohd Fahmi bin Aliman, please take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: (In Malay)   Sir, to support and encourage the spirit of volunteerism, it is important that incumbent efforts are coordinated between public agencies and community organisations.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: The DIAN Ambassadors Program was launched to support families residing in rental flats by understanding their needs and aspirations to help uplift their situation.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: How do Project DIAN Ambassadors support their target families?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Are there resources that Project DIAN Ambassadors can tap on, so that they can better engage these families, and are these resources sufficient?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: If not, could more support be provided to ensure that our ambassadors can run this program better?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: (In Malay):   Sir, in building a Malay/Muslim Community of Success, it would be important for us to further strengthen our social compact.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: One way to do this would be for the Government to work closely together with the community partners.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Last year, at AMP 4th National Convention, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance, Lawrence Wong noted that Malay/Muslim organisations need to collaborate strongly with one another, as well as the Government, to address social issues that are increasingly becoming complex.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: With the formation of M3, it seeks to harness strengths from the three agencies, mobilise community assets & resources as well as collaborate with Government agencies & Malay/Muslim organisations to address the community's challenges, particularly in the area of last mile service delivery.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: The establishment of M3 is step in the right direction as coordination and resources are amalgamated to better serve our community.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Therefore, how can we expand the network of community partners to better serve the needs of the M3 beneficiaries?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Sharael Taha, please take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In Malay):   Sir, a good education remains fundamental to helping both individuals and families achieve success and social mobility.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Therefore, it is important for the youth to have access to education.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While the more affluent have access to supplementary classes like private tuition, the lower income families may not be able to afford it.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Hence, MENDAKI has played an important role in helping lower income Malay/Muslim children and youths in this regard.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How have MENDAKI programmes such as KelasMateMatika and the MENDAKI Tuition Scheme been successful in enabling our children and youths to fulfil their educational potential?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In Malay):   At the M3 Forum held in February, we saw how the 11 M3 towns rolled out many initiatives to uplift the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As each town has different demographics and is unique, M3 volunteers have tweaked and designed programmes around the four Focus Areas to meet the needs of our community in the towns.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We will continue to monitor their academic performance over the year.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: All these initiatives to uplift the community is only possible through the efforts of its volunteers, who come from all walks of life.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Some of them have benefitted from MENDAKI initiatives and programmes, such as scholarships, bursaries, awards presented to students for their achievements.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How can we encourage more youth to join as volunteers and contribute back to the community?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: (In Malay)   Sir, flagship programs such as the MENDAKI Tuition Scheme and KelasMatematika are now well known in the community, serving students across all levels from preschool to university.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: A hallmark of the MENDAKI programs has been the mobilization of volunteers and the community, to bring up the community.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: In other words, it instills the spirit of cooperation and sense of ownership in the effort to achieve progress for our Malay-Muslim community.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: While progress is being made, we must keep pushing ourselves to achieve even more.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: How can we do more to reduce the barriers that prevent students and parents from enrolling in the programs and getting the most out of it.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: How can we further improve the quality and consistency of our community engagement?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: How can we do more to support our children even earlier in their educational journey?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: How can we continue to work with our community, and also cooperate with other communities to pool resources and do joint projects for our mutual benefit?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: How do we respond to the shifts that the education system will go through moving forward?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: (In Malay):   Sir, mentoring programmes provide emotional support and career guidance to mentees so that they can achieve their aspirations.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: Last year I was quite happy when my younger sibiling who was studying at university told me about signing up to be a peer mentor with MENDAKI.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: Mentors can help their mentees to overcome life challenges and give career guidance to assist them in their professional lives.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: One youth mentoring programme is the #amPowered Programme.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: What are the timeline and plans for the #amPowered Programme to be expanded to all M3@Towns and ITEs, to make it more accessible to the community?

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Chairman, our Malay/Muslim community has played an integral part in our nation-building.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Generations of community and religious leaders toiled alongside our fellow countrymen to build Singapore.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It is this spirit of citizenry that has carried us far as a society, where everyone steps forward and contributes.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We strive to build a Community of Success based on "three Cs": Character, Competency and Citizenry.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I shared how we strengthened our character and developed our competency in previous Committee of Supply debates.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This year, I will share about the third "C", Citizenry.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Citizenry comes from a sense of belonging and responsibility to Singapore – our country and its people.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It is about coming together to build a better future, being confident in our abilities to make positive changes and showing care for one another.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: By being active citizens, we become a vibrant and contributing community who uplift those around us, forging a stronger Singapore.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: (In Malay):   Our theme this year is "Contributing Citizens, Stronger Nation".

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It reflects our roles and obligations to one another as citizens of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This theme exemplifies the spirit of the Forward Singapore movement where the Government rallies Singaporeans to come together to strengthen our social compact.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: A core pillar of our social compact is the role of the family.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It is through the family that we learn how to take care and fulfil our obligations to one another.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Hence, the family provides the foundation to nurture and develop a sincere sense of collective responsibility, one that binds us as our fellow citizens.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This sense of collective responsibility drives us to be contributing members of the community and society.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This, in turn, strengthens trust between one another.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: During MSF's COS Debate, I spoke about the three “S” for all families – Stability, Self-Reliance, and Social Mobility.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They understood the importance of education in uplifting our community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Today, the education levels in our community are higher.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: More families have been able to achieve stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In the journey towards success, our community does not leave behind our cultural and religious values.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is because MUIS continues to develop our asatizah's talents and strengthen our religious infrastructure to nurture our character.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am proud of the success of our Malay/Muslim community, who are also actively contributing to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Third, expanding the community’s contributions to the nation We are committed to building stable, strong and resilient families.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain asked about initiatives that support the building of strong marriages and families.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As the saying goes, we need to go upstream if there's an issue downstream.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is due to the strong guidance and support from our Kadis and Naib Kadis (Muslim marriage solemnisers).

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They undertook learning journeys to INSPIRASI Hubs (AMP and PPIS) and PPIS Vista Sakinah last year to gain a better understanding of the challenges faced by young couples and those who remarry.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The lessons learnt helped our Kadi and Naib Kadi to provide proactive and effective support to couples.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Dr Shahira suggested including female perspectives in the Bersamamu programme.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: All religious leaders, including Kadi and Naib Kadi, are trained to provide guidance that addresses the different needs of brides and grooms.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Should couples require specialised support from specialists, they are referred to other relevant agencies and services such as PPIS, AMP and Temasek Foundation Project ARIF.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The delivery of the Bersamamu programme is further strengthened by the Marital First Responder Training Programme.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This programme empowers members of the community to support couples with marital issues.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Faisal Manap asked how we can support individuals struggling with issues of gender identity.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In matters relating to religion and morality, we should refer to the Mufti and our asatizah.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They have guided us to extend our kindness to one another, including to these individuals.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is on top of the training for asatizah who serve in the education and counselling sectors so that they can provide effective support to these individuals and their families.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: All these community efforts will further strengthen our national programmes that seek to support the building of strong families.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Senior Minister of State Zaqy will elaborate how we can further contribute to society by developing our competencies.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The spirit of self-help and gotong-royong has always been deeply rooted in our community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As the Malay saying goes, "We carry the burden together regardless of its weight".

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This spirit of collaboration was the driving force that established the M3 network and various Malay/Muslim organisation (MMOs).

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The MMOs provide programmes that not only benefit the Malay/Muslim community, but also the broader society.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Minister Maliki will elaborate on the contributions of our MMOs in his speech.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To empower our MMOs, among others, we must continue to support and strengthen their leadership core.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Ms Nadia asked about efforts to develop our future community leaders.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This includes building networks and synergy with others, which will help the community more effectively and systematically.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I have personally heard the ideas from these leaders which are not only refreshing, but also emphasise synergy in collaboration.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our religious leaders also play an important role in guiding the community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: ICCOS offers a construct of how we, as a minority Muslim community, can contribute to the peace and prosperity of our nation.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Saktiandi's queries, MUIS is developing a body of religious knowledge to empower our asatizah to guide the community confidently and contribute to the nation.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our efforts to develop this body of religious knowledge has attracted interest from religious institutions overseas.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: During my recent visit to Egypt, the Al-Azhar University and Egypt’s Dar Al-Ifta expressed their support to Singapore's efforts.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They also expressed interest to work with MUIS to develop this body of knowledge.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: One of the pioneer research fellows of the RPCS is Ustaz Fathurrahman Dawoed.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: He studied the factors that contributed to an observed over-reliance on halal certification.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: His research findings help our asatizah to guide the community to preserve our common spaces.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This will facilitate social mixing and forge trust between different religious groups, while upholding our religious principles.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MUIS will provide greater support to the RCPS research fellows to develop Singapore's future religious leaders and thinkers.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They will be given training opportunities in research methodologies and data visualisation, along with mentorship with esteemed local and international experts.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Muis will also establish a digital repository later this year.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It will contain resources on Islamic and social sciences covering emerging issues related to Governance, Society, Science and Technology.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This repository will help our asatizah provide religious guidance with conviction and able to address contemporary issues in society.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: On matters related to religion, Mr Faisal Manap asked for an update on the wearing of the tudung in the uniformed services.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These officers wield armed force and enforce the laws of Singapore, and are secular arms of the State.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Therefore, they must always be seen to be fair and impartial and performing their duty without fear or favour.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is especially important when responding to incidents that have racial or religious undertones.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Dr Shahira asked how our madrasah graduates can continue serving as asatizah and contribute to the religious development of the community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: There are currently over 600 undergraduates pursuing degrees in Islamic Studies and related programmes overseas.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: After undergoing the Postgraduate Certificate in Islam in Contemporary Societies (PCICS) programme and certified under the Asatizah Recognition Scheme (ARS), they can teach or work at religious institutions such as MUIS, Syariah Court, madrasah and mosques.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MUIS is also studying how to connect these graduates to the relevant institutions.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MUIS will share more details later this year.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To Dr Shahira’s query on the Singapore Community Wakaf (WMS), the WMS will support the long-term needs of the Muslim community, including our religious institutions and the development of our asatizah.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The WMS will garner funds mainly from legacy planning and planned giving by the community, hence does not compete with MMOs who mainly fundraise for ad-hoc donations.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: (In English): Dr Wan Rizal asked how our religious leaders can extend their contributions to benefit wider society.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Besides guiding the community, they play an important role in providing solutions to current issues in society and rallying the community for the common good.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Fatwa Committee led by the Mufti Dr Nazirudin was conferred the Al-Qarafi Award last year by the General Secretariat for Fatwa Authorities Worldwide from Dar Al-Ifta, the prestigious religious authority in Egypt.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This was in recognition of the Mufti and the Fatwa Committee's strong leadership and outstanding contributions in guiding the community on various contemporary issues during the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The emphasis on peaceful co-existence in their religious guidance was also recognised by international religious scholars.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Thus far, I have shared how we build strong families and strong leaders.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These two pillars strengthen each other and provide an enabling environment for our community to thrive and contribute to the nation.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In this regard, I agree with Mr Saktiandi and Ms Mariam that we must not only thrive as a community, but actively give back to the larger society.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Many professional bodies, such as lawyers, doctors and educators, are helping to uplift the community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They partnered MENDAKI to guide our Malay/Muslim students on career pathways in the aviation industry and have since extended their programme to Singapore Indian Development Association (SINDA) to benefit other communities.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Many Malay/Muslims, having done well for themselves, are also contributing at the national level.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: He also mentors youths pursuing careers in science and conducts outreach to vulnerable families.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Her efforts help to address our national concern of combatting extremism.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Abu Bakar Mohd Nor is Chairman of M Kapital Holdings.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: He was previously Chairman of M3@Tampines but has since widened his contributions by serving at the national level as Chairman of the Tampines Central Citizen Consultative Committee.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These individuals do not just inspire us with their success, but also their deep commitment to uplifting others.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our community's contributions across various sectors in society, is something we should celebrate and be proud of.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Indeed, we are a community that live by the ethos of Rahmatan Lil Alamin, or "Blessings to All", actively seeking to build bridges to reach out to those beyond our own.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They worked with various partners, such as temples, churches, mosques and the Singapore Association for the Visually Handicapped to pack and distribute essential items for families.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: RLAF not only reached out to the vulnerable but cultivated stronger bonds among Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Many have become successful and progressed in life.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I encourage them to give back to the community and keep the spirit of care and citizenry.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Through M3, professionals and volunteers from all walks of lives lend their expertise and skills to help the community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: While we pursue our aspirations, let us remain connected with those around us, like our neighbours and the wider community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: All of us have a role to play in uplifting the community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It is when each of us become active citizens that we become a community where we are each other's keeper – looking out for one another, extending a helping hand.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: So, I urge everyone to step forward to uplift others.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We can only build a stronger Singapore, together.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, as our Malay/Muslim community continues to progress forward, we strive to capitalise our assets and facilitate active citizenry within the community, to look beyond our own needs and contribute to greater causes.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To do this, we will nurture a strong ecosystem of giving back in the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, we will improve coordination across public agencies and community organisations.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, we will develop a strong volunteer corps with the right knowledge and skillset.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: And third, we will build a strong network of community partners for broader and deeper impact in the community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In Malay):   Our community is united in supporting the vulnerable group and are constantly finding better ways to uplift them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Often times these families face complex issues that require support from many different government and non-Government agencies.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Through Project DIAN, we focus on three groups of families who stay in HDB rental flats.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, the elderly who live alone; second, middle-aged parents with adult children, or multi-generational families; and third, and young families with young children.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The third group of young families is our key priority.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They have an average of three children or more, with the mean age of the oldest and youngest children at 11 and four years old respectively.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Some even have children who are even younger.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: During our house visits, we further observed that some children demonstrate developmental delays.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Some also, did not attend preschool or missed school regularly.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Fahmi asked how the DIAN Ambassadors support the target families and are equipped to engage this group.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The DIAN Ambassadors will visit the families fortnightly to read with the child and engage them in activities that allows the child to play while learning which assists in the child’s cognitive and social skills development.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The DIAN Ambassadors will also involve the young parents, to empower them to support their children in early childhood education.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We work closely with the Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) to plan the curriculum and educational materials for the children, as well as to implement a robust programme evaluation approach.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To measure the progress of each family, SUSS systematically evaluates the case notes recorded by our DIAN Ambassadors at every visit, and will conduct interviews with family members to better understand their situation.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Additionally, KidSTART helps to train our DIAN Ambassadors on early childhood development to enable them to effectively interact with these children and provide appropriate intervention.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Dr Wan Rizal asked for an update on Project DIAN.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: However, the journey for our DIAN ambassadors has not been easy.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Some face challenges in fostering trust with the families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Nevertheless, they persevere and give their best effort for the young children in these families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Having said that, Chairman, we do have some early success and are confident that this programme brings about tangible impact on the lives of some of these Project DIAN families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, through Project DIAN, Siti (not her real name), a housewife, was referred to the e2i and NTUC to improve her employment opportunity and support her family.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Siti's youngest son, aged six, benefited from our DIAN Ambassador programme through the developmental intervention.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Her child has shown progress and interest in learning new things.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Siti’s 8-year-old daughter also receives weekly tuition coordinated by the M³ Engagement Coordination Office (M³ ECO) and this 8-year old is now much more focused and confident in her schoolwork.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Chairman, the volunteers' passion is the bedrock of an active and vibrant community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To support the growth of our M³ programmes, such as Project DIAN, we will not only increase our pool of volunteers, but also ensure that each volunteer is well-supported with the knowledge and skills so that they can contribute effectively.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: M³ ECO was set up for this very purpose.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: M³ ECO has put in place a robust Volunteers' Capability Building Framework, to equip M³ volunteers with the right skillsets to engage its target group of families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Since its inception in September 2021, over 150 volunteers have gone through the training programmes.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They became more confident in engaging and building rapport with the residents.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They provide useful information to these families based on their needs.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Besides basic skills training, we also organise specialised trainings with certain Government agencies, where our volunteers are equipped with specific knowledge about Government policies and schemes that could benefit the families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our volunteers come from all walks of life, each bringing their unique experience and expertise to serve those in need.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We hope they will continue to be an inspiration to many more to step forward and join us in these programmes.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, for the impact on our community to be further broadened and deepened, it is critical that we expand and strengthen the network of community partners that give back.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman and Ms Nadia Samdin asked how we broaden our web of partners, including supporting synergies among existing organisations, as well as with new groups.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Today, our network of established Malay/Muslim Organisations (MMOs) and Indian/Muslim Organisations (IMOs) support many vulnerable segments of the community and we thank them for all their efforts.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They play an important role of corralling resources and implementing programmes to meet the diverse needs of our community and fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To Ms Nadia Samdin’s question, beyond the individual contributions that each MMO and IMO makes, they can play a greater role in community building through collaborative partnerships.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For instance, last December, the Singapore Muslim Women’s Association, or PPIS, collaborated with the Prophet Muhammad’s Birthday Memorial Scholarship Fund Board (LBKM) to launch a new postgraduate scholarship to support women in achieving their aspirations.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The scholarship is open to women pursuing further studies in STEM, community work and gerontology, among other relevant options.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This collaboration is an example of community efforts to grow more female role models within the community and we do encourage many more MMOs and IMOs to come together in partnership to offer more scholarships and programmes for the community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Beyond existing community organisations, we must also cultivate new partners to harness their influence and capabilities.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is why the other Malay/Muslim leaders and I have been actively engaging different groups to listen to their views and share avenues within the M³ framework where they can contribute.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I met close to 30 financial advisors to discuss how the Government can partner the community of financial advisers to improve the community’s financial literacy.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I was very heartened that many of them were keen to share their knowledge with residents on the ground and we invited them to conduct financial literacy talks at out M³ Towns.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Similarly, the volunteer lawyers under M³ organised legal sharing sessions for residents and guide them in applying for a Lasting Power of Attorney.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: On the medical front, the doctors and healthcare professionals from the community also stepped forward.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, Dr Fadzil Hamzah works closely with M³@Tampines and asatizahs at Ghufran Mosque to conduct talks on prenatal health.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Such collaborative partnerships between the Government and various community nodes often have a multiplier effect on the community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To strengthen and deepen synergy, we actively look into creating platforms to share ideas and strengthen ties across our network of partners.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is why we started the M³ Forum – to serve as a platform for M³ partners and volunteers to come together to take stock and reflect on past work done, while forging new insights and partnerships for the road ahead.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I urge more Muslim community groups to come forward to be part of the M³ family to reinforce a network of care for our community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, I have shared our efforts in nurturing a culture of active citizenry within the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: However, this cannot be achieved overnight, nor by the Government’s efforts alone.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Building a contributing community requires close partnerships between volunteers, public agencies and community organisations.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: And, at the heart of it, the dedication and passion of this coalition of partners towards a common goal of creating a better future for our fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, our Malay community can be proud of the significant progress that we have made over the years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As more achieve success, we must continue mobilising and rallying one another to contribute back, inspire others and help those in need.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: With this spirit of togetherness, we can overcome challenges, achieve our aspirations and lead meaningful lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To empower a capable and contributing community, we will provide a strong educational foundation for our young; nurture a strong community spirit through youth volunteerism and mentoring; and help Malay/Muslim professionals fulfil their potential and enable them to inspire others to pursue their dreams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: (In Malay):   Education remains a cornerstone for success as it opens doors to opportunities that help us reach our aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI will help our children and youth fulfil their potential by regularly improving our education and developmental programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Sharael Taha and Ms Mariam Jaafar asked about the effectiveness of MENDAKI's programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It also builds parents' confidence in assisting their children in Mathematics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is encouraging because a joint study by MENDAKI and Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) showed that a strong educational foundation in Primary 1 has a long-lasting impact and correlates to how well our students do at PSLE.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Besides early exposure to Math, KMM students will join specially curated coding camps and learning journeys to inculcate Mathematics into their everyday lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Special sessions will be organised at targeted preschool centres including all 15 mosque-based kindergartens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Another programme that has become synonymous to MENDAKI's academic efforts is the MENDAKI Tuition Scheme or MTS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: With the opening of MTS centres in the neighbourhood and more affordable fees, I hope more will join and benefit from the programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Besides academic achievements, it is important for our youth to have a good social support system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Besides their families, mentors can guide and help our youth expand their world view.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As they become more aware of available education and career pathways, we hope that they will set higher goals and work hard towards achieving their aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In my COS speech last year, I announced that the #amPowered mentoring programme will be launched in all Institutes of Technical Education (ITEs) and M³ towns progressively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin's query, the #amPowered programme are currently available at the three ITE Colleges and across three M³ towns in Jurong, Chua Chu Kang and Marsiling-Yew Tee.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: During the COVID-19 pandemic, we were forced to shift our mentoring sessions online.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This made it challenging for our youth to build strong connections with their mentors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Fortunately, from this year, the mentoring sessions can be conducted physically.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have also infused experiential learning and community building activities into our mentoring programme so that our youth can be exposed to more educational and career opportunities and be more cognisant of current issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Throughout this year, MENDAKI will organise at least one youth mentoring programme in each M³ town.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This will make it easier for our youths to sign up for the programme, no matter where they reside in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI is currently evaluating our mentoring programmes to understand how far our youth have benefited from them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Through these education and mentoring programmes, we hope our youth will excel in school and build strong foundations and network to set themselves for greater achievements in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: (In English): Uplifting a community requires each of us to play a part.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: At the centre of our education and mentoring programmes is a strong, dedicated team of volunteers who understand the needs of the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In the past three years, more than 1,000 volunteers were deployed across MENDAKI programmes to engage beneficiaries at different life stages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Therefore, our volunteers need to be equipped with the necessary skillsets and expertise to engage the beneficiaries effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One of our volunteers is Ms Nur Alwany.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Ms Alwany was a recipient of the Tertiary Tuition Fees Subsidy (TTFS) when she undertook her studies in polytechnic and then the university.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: She wanted to give back and first volunteered with MENDAKI in 2016 for the KidsRead programme and, subsequently, with KMM.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As a KMM facilitator, Ms Alwany builds her students' interest and capability in basic numeracy though fun and engaging ways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: She also encourages her students to actively participate in her class to build their self-confidence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For her dedication, MENDAKI encouraged Ms Alwany to attend a family conference by the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Through the conference, Ms Alwany gained better insights into the needs of her students and was able to apply the lessons she learnt to her role as a KMM facilitator.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I have met many like Ms Alwany, who had benefited from MENDAKI's programmes, and now feels a sense of duty to help others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am heartened by their generosity and spirit of gotong-royong.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This virtuous cycle of support will be the engine of our community's progress.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Sharael Taha asked how we can encourage more youths to come forward as volunteers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Last year, as we celebrated the achievements of our students, we made a call for them to step up and make positive contributions to the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will continue to support the passion and energy of our youths to make positive changes they want to see within their community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It is through these volunteering opportunities that our youths develop skills, discover interests, build relationships and guide others to success.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: While we create strong foundations for our young, we must also focus on supporting our Malay/Muslim workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As a community, we must continue supporting one another to improve employment and upskilling opportunities so that more can have good jobs and achieve their career goals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We established our employability networks involving agencies, such as NTUC e2i, NTUC Learning Hub, Workforce Singapore (WSG) and SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG), to better assist our Malay/Muslim workers with their employment needs, and this covers from training to upskilling to landing job placements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI has formed the Professional Networks programme for Malay/Muslim professionals to know others in their field, exchange ideas and help younger workers entering growing industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This year, MENDAKI plans to expand its Professional Networks to include other in-demand industries, such as finance, sustainability and engineering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This will create more opportunities to connect our youths with professionals who can inspire and guide them to pursue a wide range of career pathways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI also shares best practices with other MMOs through the Community Leaders' Forum (CLF) to help them deliver more effective programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Faisal Manap asked for an update on the CLF and the Malay/Muslim Community Development Fund (MMCDF).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The CLF serves as a platform to ensure efficient and effective management of resources by the various MMOs to avoid duplication of programmes and services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In 2022, more than 170 participants attended sharing sessions on programme evaluation, volunteer management and governance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This provided an opportunity for CLF partners to come together to contribute to the learning and development of best practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Since 2013, the MMCDF has been expanded to support project implementation and organisational development efforts of our MMOs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Through the MMCDF, CLF provides funding support for our MMOs to develop and implement programmes that uplift the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The programme empowers individuals from less-privileged households by equipping them with trade and business skills to start or enhance their home-based business as an additional source of income.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Beyond projects, MMCDF also supports initiatives to groom the next generation of leaders of our MMOs through the Tunas Bersama M3 programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is our way to build capacity because these are leaders who will be at the helm of the MMOs in charting the community's way forward in the near future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI will continue to work with the Government, fellow Malay/Muslim organisations, sector leaders and employees to ramp up efforts to empower the community, whether through M3 or through CLF, to gain good employment and, together, support all our community members who are in need.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister Masagos, Minister Maliki and I have spoken on the theme of Contributing Citizens, Stronger Nation, and how we intend to strengthen the foundation of the family, nurture future religious and community leaders, and expand the community's contributions to the nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As new challenges emerge, we must continue to build up and leverage our community support, knowledge and resources to become a Community of Success.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As the saying goes, alone we can do so little, together we can do so much more.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am confident that our Malay/Muslim community will continue to forge forward as one and contribute towards the prosperity of the nation.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We will take clarifications on this topic now – about 10 to 15 minutes of clarification time – because the other MCCY political office holders (POHs) also have to respond to the cuts.

speaker: The Chairman
text: So, could I invite Members, if there are any clarifications?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: One, on the International Conference on Communities of Success (ICCOS).

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Moving forward, we also need to look at the online spaces, be it social media or online gaming platforms, which are the new frontier in the jostle for influence and ideologies.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: So, perhaps MUIS and its foreign counterparts can consider strategies to occupy this space and perhaps have a permanent ICCOS online platform for this.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Second, on strengthening the foundation of families, I thank the Minister for the comprehensive reply.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Lately, we read about a family violence case against a young child.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: There are blended families – single parents, unwed mothers, grandparents or elder siblings – playing the parenting role.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Are there any focus areas, perhaps consolidated focus areas, on this group of our community so that we do not forget them, perhaps focusing on parenting skills and working together with organisations like PPIS, AMP or BAPA?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Many of them live in similar conditions like ourselves – as minorities in secular, progressive countries and protected by law, bound by the Constitution.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is one area where we can find synergy and work with similar communities.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
