text: And the Families for Life Council (FFL) is on the ground and going to expand national programmes, and I hope that whatever background we come from – from whatever communities – we tap on these national initiatives.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: At the same time, we will support those that have special needs, whether it is about family violence or relationship issues, FAM@FSC or Strengthening Families Programme@Family Service Centre, will provide them.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And then at the third layer, we also want and have been engaging Malay/Muslim organisations to provide culturally-nuanced and even religiously effective ways of addressing the issues, in addition to those that are given at the national level.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: Senior Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad earlier mentioned that the #amPowered programme will be progressively rolled out across all the ITEs and M3@Towns.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Certainly, we are always on the lookout for partners to help us expand the breadth and width of our programmes, especially to help our young be exposed to what is out there in the market so that they have some sense of what is needed, guided to pursue such careers, as well as being able to see the companies in action.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: MSD Pharma is one of the biggest pharmaceutical companies in Singapore and rated one of the best employers in the country since 2020.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Through these programmes, our ITE students will receive guidance on how they can prepare themselves and be given a chance at maybe interning or visiting some of their factories or manufacturing plants.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Moving forward, we look forward to more partnerships where we can expose our kids through various platforms.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: If any of you know of anyone who is interested, you can always refer corporates and partners to us, especially entrepreneurs and even SMEs to give our kids a chance to be exposed.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, yes, this is one way in which we want our kids to fulfil their potential.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Is MENDAKI looking at more scholarships with the private sector, in order to create more stronger mentorship programmes for our Malay/Muslim youths?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The short answer is yes, we take what we can get.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But I hope that we can certainly garner more who are interested to help uplift members of the community.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These are ways in which corporates can give back and I hope that we can get more on board.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We also got entrepreneurs too, like, Ismail Gafoor, who has also put in funds to support our young kids who need additional coaching in Maths, for example.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, there are ways in which corporates, large and small, who are doing their part to help uplift the community.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: One to Minister, with regard to the gedung-gedung ilmu, the repository for information resource for the asatizahs.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: I think it is a wonderful initiative and programme to step up our asatizahs.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Can Minister share a bit more about how we can extend it even further, beyond the subject matter and also beyond this year into next year?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: And related to that, what does it mean for the asatizahs' wages going forward?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Does it help enhance their professionalism and does it also encourage more young people to go into that area as well, moving forward?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: My second question is with regard to what Minister mentioned just now, the example of professionals like Malay/Muslim pilots coming forward to help as a body.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Can Minister share a bit more on the efforts to gather more professional groups to help the community?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: And like he mentioned, helping even SINDA, going forward as well.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: He shared individuals and those are mostly locals, but the other element is also scouring more for overseas Malay/Muslims who have done very well abroad, brought Singapore's brand name to greater heights and —

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Saktiandi, could I ask you to ask your clarifications.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: When I broached this idea with the Mufti of Egypt, the scholars from Morocco, the vice dean of al-Qarawiyyin University, which is the oldest university of the Muslim world, as well as the Sheikh of Al-Azhar, they were very supportive and think that this is one area that we must develop more.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: There is already a basic foundational knowledge on these issues on how to approach them.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have gathered religious leaders now who have interest to contribute to this body of knowledge, through their research.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We now have really interesting books that they have contributed and never found applications for, and they now say, "wow, this is exactly what I wrote these books for".

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I mentioned one person, but he was leading a group of pilots who were interested to motivate, mentor ITE students, to inspire them to go beyond whatever they are studying, to be able to fly, even if they are starting with a simulator.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This was an initiative that was broached by them, and I never even thought about it and I thought it was a wonderful way of the pilots, dressed in their uniform, motivating our students.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I see many of them, eyes really light up when they sit in the cockpit simulator.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Yes, I agree with the Member that there are many more professionals, even entrepreneurs, people who have gone overseas.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: You have great ideas that can motivate and inspire our community, but as I mentioned in my speech, let us also contribute beyond.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Let us also use these ideas, the expertise to also contribute to those who need it and they may not necessarily come from our community – like the pilots have done for SINDA.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: I have seen the efforts, I think it is fantastic.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: In my cut, I mentioned some potential challenges in terms of manpower and coordination.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: Perhaps Minister can share what are the plans to mitigate this.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Chairman, I thank Dr Wan Rizal for his question.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Indeed, it is not an easy effort to bring about the coordination to help groups of families which are living in very difficult circumstances.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: The first thing is we set out to understand the structures and process that need to be put in place.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: For structures, it is essentially what Dr Wan Rizal is speaking of.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We created a steering committee made up of agency representatives.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: With this coordination effort, we brought it down to all the pilot towns and each pilot town has similar steering committees that has been established.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: This is so that the staffers at the local level coordinate, understand each other, understand each case that needs to be supported.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Within Project Dian, we have a group of volunteers.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: The challenge is to get as many volunteers as we can because we literally were looking at knocking on every door of our Malay/Muslim households to understand their circumstances and the way they live.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: The older folks who have been there for many years, the children who have moved out and from there, we look at the welfare and well-being of this group.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: The coordination happens between SSO and MUIS to ensure that they are supported.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: The middle group are the ones who are middle aged with young adult children with potential for home ownership.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: For that we work with agencies like e2i, MENDAKI, to create opportunities for us to upskill and upgrade the adults, so that they can possibly find good jobs, increase their economic potential to be able to be home owners.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: The third group is the one that I mentioned earlier, that requires a lot more attention.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: These are the young families, young families who are married and did not have the means to purchase their homes yet.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Within that space, we also want to make sure that we support the children.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: These young families have got a number of children, three to five children.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: That is really where the volunteers, the Dian ambassadors, come in actively, and they have been trained to help these families.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Dr Wan Rizal is right, we need a lot of manpower and that is why in my speech, I spoke about the call for more of Singaporeans out there, regardless whether you are Malay, Muslim or not, if you have the heart to want to help families in rental flats, help the children, uplift them, work together with us and join us.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Still on Dian and my question to Minister Maliki.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: When I really look at it, it is a great success.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: We have a very strong network in terms of using KidSTART and MENDAKI assets to help the preschool and children in early education.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: But in terms of madrasah education, I think there is a gap.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Just wondering if there are any plans to get assistance to help our youths or our students in madrasahs to keep up in their own studies.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: I think we support all the children in our Project Dian families, regardless of which school they are attending.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We refer them to MENDAKI's weekend tuition programmes.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We also have got volunteers who are prepared to do home-based tutoring and we have done that.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We have a group of mentors from the IHLs who have already been recruited.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Usually, what we do is when there is a request and we realise that there is a student in one of the rental flat homes, we will assess their need for educational support and we will look for the most suitable way of supporting them, even if it is home-based tuition.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: That is where we then tap on the pool of volunteers that we have.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: If it is centre-based weekend support, we then refer them to MENDAKI tuition programmes.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: So, this help is available regardless of where they go to school.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Then, we will carry on with the Committee of Supply for Head X.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Chairman, since 2011, I have been holding monthly KopiTalk sessions in a food court in Tampines North.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: For two hours each time, residents and members of the public can join and participate in the conversation.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: The refreshments offered do attract some interest, but I believe that the discussion also gave us a lot of food for thought.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Participants can raise any topics on top of their mind, and I will give my take and share what I know.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Anyone present can also chip in to add to the discussion.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: I find it very useful to know what people are thinking of, worried about and concerned with, as well as their views and opinions on estate matters, current topics and national issues.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Last month's session was held a few days after Budget Day.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: I used the opportunity to share the key parts of the Budget and what residents can look forward to.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Besides such topical matters, what I found most useful is when we discuss community issues like corridor clutter, cat and bird feeding, noise pollution and so on where the community needs to come together to solve problems.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: On a much larger level and wider platform, we have initiatives like Forward Singapore exercise and Singapore Together movement over the past few years.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, please take your two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Mr Chairman, I had raised at last year’s MCCY COS, about the Arts and Heritage Plans, which identified the priorities for Singapore’s arts and heritage development for 2018 to 2022.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: As 2022 marked the end of the first phase of the plans, I had sought an update from the Ministry on the next iteration of the plans.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: For MCCY’s Heritage Plan 2.0, I recall the direction was to enhance the heritage sector’s digital capabilities, showcase Singapore’s rich multicultural heritage beyond our shores to grow new audiences and markets for the sector and to work closely with our local communities and heritage enthusiasts and partners in the tech and creative industries to celebrate our unique local histories.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: I therefore invite MCCY to update us on its refreshed Arts and Heritage Plans 2.0 for the next lap, show how the public and stakeholder consultations have shaped these plans, and also expand on MCCY’s efforts to increase arts access to various demographics in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Mr Chairman, our National Monuments in Singapore form an indelible and integral part of our built heritage.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: These National Monuments preserve not only our history but a quick look at the list of National Monuments shows that quite clearly it also represents in many ways the unique social compact that we have built as a society.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: The Padang, the latest addition to the list needs no introduction as to the historical significance it holds for pre and post independent Singapore.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Sultan Mosque, Sri Mariamman Temple, St Andrews Cathedral and Tian Hock Keng (天福宫) represent a short list of the many National Monuments that showcase the collective conscience of our Nation, as a multiracial, multicultural and multireligious society where Singaporeans of diverse cultural backgrounds and beliefs live harmoniously together as fellow citizens.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Is the Ministry co-creating a vision in the medium term with the sector?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: It is, therefore, critical that the sector also grows and develops new capabilities in order to provide and create exciting new opportunities for our future talent.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Can the Ministry share its plans in this regard to support the sector?

text: (In Mandarin)   Mr Chairman, globally, the ongoing China-US rivalry and the Ukraine war, as well as global economic slowdown and uncertainty will affect Singapore negatively.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Even if the Government works out a strategy, we may not be able to turn the tide.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Hence, global uncertainty will inevitably have a negative impact on Singapore.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: During last year's debate, the Government announced that it would actively engage the community to promote arts and culture in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Today, a year later, what are the new developments in the Government's plans?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: How does the Government ensure that Singaporeans, young and old, can access and appreciate arts?

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
text: We have always had a diverse societyand shared heritage provides that common space for all of us, regardless of race, language or religion.

text: For new citizens, heritage, culture and the arts can help to anchor them to Singapore and to adopt our national identity.

text: Could the Minister elaborate on MCCY's vision and plans over the next five years for the development of Singapore arts and culture?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Mr Chairman, I use dialects routinely when I communicate with many of my residents every day and many of them are middle-aged to elderly residents.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: But I have also observed that in many families, most young children do not understand dialects.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: At best, a small number may understand dialects as they hear their grandparents communicate with them in dialects.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The MCCY has previously affirmed that Chinese dialects are part of the Singapore Chinese culture and heritage.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: As part of the different Chinese migrant groups coming to Singapore in the early years of Singapore, our forefathers come from different parts of Southern China and brought their different dialects to Singapore, together with the dialect group culture.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Our dialect group heritage is part of our Singaporean Chinese cultural heritage.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Beyond the speaking of dialect, it is important to preserve knowledge among all Singaporean Chinese of the cultural heritage of our dialect groups, which may include culture, customs and food.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: How many of our young Singaporeans have good knowledge of the cultural practices of their dialect group?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Recently, I asked a 13-year-old student, what is his dialect group.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: He shrugged his shoulders and said that he did not know.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: With an ageing population and a younger generation who have a limited exposure to dialect, we are reaching a tipping point.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Transferring culture and heritage does not happen overnight and the runway to do so is growing ever shorter.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Once this culture and heritage dies off, there is no way of re-building it.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: We should ask ourselves whether we can do more to preserve this intangible heritage.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I applaud the existing efforts of many of our clan associations in the promotion of the use of dialects as well as the customs, practices and culture of our dialect groups despite the modern cultural challenges.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Can the Government do more to enhance the learning and speaking of dialects as well as promoting the knowledge of our customs, practices and culture of our various dialect groups among younger Singaporeans?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Chairman, over the past years, numerous art spaces have been added to our cityscape.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Today, we can see street art at Haji Lane, Far East Square and Joo Chiat.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We have also been more experimental with different formats of art presentation, for example, iLight and Night Festival.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Various interest groups have also organised their own independent art events.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Each of these have added vibrancy and flavour to our cityscape, creating additional opportunities for Singaporeans to come together and enjoy art and culture.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Not only that, but they also have given our art practitioners additional spaces and opportunities to explore their diverse talents and be more experimental with their art forms.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Art spaces will continue to grow in importance especially in an increasingly pluralistic society where pursuits of interest can be very diverse and when our fellow Singaporeans seek different ways to express themselves creatively and artistically.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Can MCCY share their intentions to provide more art spaces for our practitioners to experiment with different forms of art and art presentation?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And how does the Ministry intend to inject more vibrancy into the cultural landscape by making art more accessible to Singaporeans?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Apart from Passion Art events, are there plans for MCCY to create permanent art spaces in the heartlands or to bring experimental art forms to the neighbourhoods so that Singaporeans can immerse in art closer to where they live?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The precinct has been envisaged as a one-stop destination for Singaporeans to enjoy community sports, as well as world class entertainment and events.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Sports Hub is an important centrepiece in the development of the precinct and has been envisaged to serve as a focal point for international sports and entertainment events, as well as a social sporting venue for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I believe that Minister Edwin Tong had shared this in Parliament last year.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There have also been some concerns regarding how Sports Hub will balance the needs of different communities while operating the Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Could the Government please share how SportsSG would balance the desire to host international sports and entertainment events at Sports Hub, while ensuring that it is still accessible to Singaporeans for community sports and also for community events as well?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan, please take both your cuts together.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Minister has also affirmed the Government's commitment to continue doing so.

text: Mr Mark Chay, please take both your cuts together.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: I will be the first to state that as a tenant of Kallang Wave Mall, there have been visible improvements in some areas.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: But, overall, I feel that there is a change in the vibrancy and energy of the precinct.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: Not long ago, the Sports Hub felt like a ghost town, unless Jay Chou was performing.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: Today, programmes are organised for participants of all interests every day of the week.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: The public can access sports and fitness classes, rent equipment and use world-class facilities to pursue their sporting ambitions.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: The events calendar looks vibrant, and many community events, local and international sports competitions and concerts are planned in the coming months.

text: KSAM is already delivering on its promise of more opportunities for locals to compete in and use its facilities.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: It has been four years since that has happened.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: With so much optimism and potential linked with the Sports Hub and KASM, I would like to raise the following points.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: One, many of the facilities are used by the National Sports Associations (NSAs) for national team training.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: Two, I would like to encourage event organisers to, as far as possible, organise events after office hours or on the weekends for the very simple reason of making it easy for parents, who are their children's biggest fans, to watch their kids compete and perform.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: It would go a long way in growing Singapore's sporting culture.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: Three, Sir, I spend a lot of time at the Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: I also spent a lot of time in SportsSG.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: An observation I would like to share is that people enjoy going to the Sports Hub simply because it is a lovely open venue to play.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: I believe KASM's can and should do more to promote the ease of use of its facilities and it should explore collaboration with private vendors to increase the reach to the public.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: Instead of trying to deliver all programmes, I would encourage KASM to work with the existing tenants and NSAs to provide community programmes.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: First, I would like to ask MCCY to provide an update on sports facilities planned for upgrading as part of the Masterplan.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: Second, as our society matures, can MCCY share how it plans to make these facilities accessible for persons with disabilities (PwDs) and the elderly?

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: And third, can MCCY share its plans to collaborate with NSAs to use the facilities for training and competition during off-peak hours?

text: How will all these pathways fit to ensure that we have enough young talents playing together at the right level and standard?

text: Are they performing well in the national schools game?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: To support all the different talent development pipelines, there needs to be sufficient and proficient training, staff and coaches.

text: Do we have the right quantity and quality of training staff and coaches?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Are there enough development opportunities for our local coaches, such as training and overseas development?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: Since that time, however, the performance of our men's national football team has been inconsistent.

text: They went from winning hearts for their never-say-die performance in 2021 ASEAN Football Federation Championship to crushing disappointment that followed their dismal exit from the 2022 tournament.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I appreciate that it will take time to grow the ecosystem that will foster young talents and develop the skills of our local coaches and footballers, more than the two years since Unleash The Roar was announced.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: In a recent podcast posted by Berita Harian, a former national player called for greater involvement of former players in developing the programmes for our local football scene.

text: He also called for, amongst other things, a dialogue session among all stakeholders, setting achievable milestones for our youth teams and creating an environment for local coaches so that they can focus on coaching and not need to moonlight.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I believe that these are all sensible recommendations.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: This implies that a healthy lifestyle driven by the active lifestyle is essential in improving longevity and minimising healthcare causes.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: The study also noted that although people in Singapore tended to be less active as compared to other groups.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Therefore, can MCCY share its plans to enhance sports participation, especially amongst groups, which may have a lower rate of participation.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Would MCCY also elaborate on how it aims to encourage groups, such as seniors and young children who may be less active in sports, to participate regularly in sports?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Over the years, Woodlands Sports Complex has become indispensable community spaces where Marsiling and Woodgrove residents who often go to.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Its facilities cater to the needs of all age groups, playing an important part in bonding the family and community closer together.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We often see parents bringing their little ones to the swimming pool for waterplay.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many friendships have been forged amongst the seniors too in these venues, be it through sports or by participating in the Active Green Harvest at the community garden located right next to the swimming pool.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I must credit ActiveSG for being a strong community partner of Marsiling-Yew Tee GRC with whom we regularly collaborate to organise a series of community events that keep our residents active.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Take the Sporting Wednesday at Woodland Stadium, for example, which encourages our Marsiling and Woodgrove residents to visit the stadium every Wednesday, from 7.00 pm to 9.00 pm to participate in a series of sports, such as walking football and so on, along with fitness programmes, such as zumba, entirely free-of-charge.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How can the Ministry, ensure that community sports are more accessible to all especially for our senior citizens and to create more opportunities for family bonding as well as fostering a shared community spirit?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Could SportsSG also work closely with MOE to explore opening up more school sports facilities to the public?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This space has great potential to be another community sporting venue, allowing residents to have more options without the need to travel all the way to the Woodlands Sports Complex.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Our youths are our country's young sprouts who will grow up to be tall oak trees to provide shelter to our communities and nation.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Our youths have demonstrated amazing resilience and adaptability, amidst the challenges and pressures of COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: They have demonstrated tenacity and a strong passion to act on issues that they care about.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In Punggol, our youths have used their own pocket money to 3D Print face shields for the community during COVID-19 and our youth networks have gone door-to-door to encourage residents to recycle well.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In fact, data from the National Youth Survey shows that 90% of youths view contributing to society as an important life goal.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Let us work together to give our youths opportunities to become leaders who are confident and committed to Singapore and who have the heart to serve.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Can MCCY share on the opportunities for youths to further develop their leadership skills, build strong networks and be involved in civic participation?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: As an integral part of our population, youths should certainly have a say in how Singapore charts our future.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: To do so, it is critical that our youths understand the key issues affecting Singapore, how different groups of fellow Singaporeans could have very different but no less important needs, how policies and legislations are formulated and the difficult trade-offs involved in such formulations.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Such understanding will enable them to think more critically, be less susceptible to potentially biased opinions perpetuated by how social media algorithms are designed and make informed decisions for themselves.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: At present, we have a range of youth dialogues organised by various Government and private entities.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: But I believe that it is important to offer our youths a structured and more hands-on programme that facilitates deeper understanding of how policy makers think, how legislations are formulated, how other countries deal with similar issues, how is Singapore unique or maybe not so unique and what do we need to give up if we choose one priority over the other.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: In this vein, would the Government consider reinstating the National Youth Forum or create the likes of it?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Their support for youths and education is especially noteworthy.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They also build mutual understanding and strengthen bonds across different ethnic groups while preserving their own cultural practices and traditions which make Singapore's heritage so rich, diverse and interesting.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What are MCCY's plans to engage our self-help groups and deepen collaborative efforts so as to strengthen cohesion among our communities?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Neighbours are generally considerate and look out for one another.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, there is an increase in the number of disputes in recent years, with the common causes being noise disruptions, smoking, littering, hoarding, just to name a few.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: At our COS debate last year, Minister Tong shared that the Community Dispute Management Framework (CDMF) was in the process of being enhanced.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I support this as it is better for neighbours to first discuss their problems in the presence of a trained mediator early instead of allowing the situation to escalate.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Some of the disputes have not been resolved for a long time, to the distress of neighbours.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Chairman, harmonious neighbourhoods are what we all hope for and work towards.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: While we work towards minimising such disputes, we must also pay attention to improving the ways we manage disputes such as the CDMF.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: In the Committee of Supply 2022, MCCY announced that the CDMF was being enhanced.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: In addition to establishing guidance to encourage self-management of the disputes, the availability of legislative levers to the Government is also important, especially for cases where self-management is unsuccessful.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Perhaps to enhance CDMF, we should not only focus on efficacy and efficiency of managing disputes but also be sensitive to the fact that, neighbours in dispute more often than not will remain as neighbours.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: The mending and improving of relationships post-CDMF should also be one of the framework's key considerations.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Can MCCY shares its plans for managing disputes under the proposed CDMF?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan, you can take both cuts, please.

text: We need clear principles to resolve disputes in a fair and balanced way, resolve these as early as possible, and yet preserve the agency and central role of residents themselves to manage the affairs within the community, while also supporting them with processes, resources and rules of the road that are more fit for purpose today.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Can MCCY update on its work on the Community Dispute Management Framework?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But it is not enough to just increase the number of volunteers.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The challenge is sustaining their interest and engaging them meaningfully.

text: We can imagine the coordination, administrative and IT support that this group needs.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Without these resources, the matching process will be less efficient, the volunteers may not be activated as often as they would like to, to sustain their interest.

text: Different volunteer centres will have varying resource support requirements.
