speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, I want to thank all the Members for their continued support for MCCY's work.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our work spans many sectors: arts, heritage, sports, youth, our community, volunteerism.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And these are all threads which bind us to one another and give us a shared stake in building Singapore together.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This unity has enabled us to achieve success as a country and also to be able to bounce back from crises.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As Mr Sitoh Yoh Pin pointed out, Singapore's social compact is based on building a diverse yet cohesive Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Baey Yam Keng also spoke about citizens coming together to solve problems at a community and also at a national level.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It was precisely to strengthen our civic bonds that we launched Singapore Together in 2019.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It marked a shift towards deeper partnerships between the Government and Singaporeans and also amongst Singaporeans themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We engaged Singaporeans on national issues like women's development and also on our long-term land use plan, and partnered them to develop solutions on complex issues through citizens' panels and Alliances for Action.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Forward Singapore extends this collaborative style of governance to further the shifts needed to strengthen our social compact, because a sustainable social compact requires the investment and also the co-ownership of all of us in society.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And perhaps, more importantly, what each of us is willing to do, to get us there.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The contributions of Singaporeans will shape and strengthen the eventual recommendations and the outcomes of Forward Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Under the Unite Pillar, our focus is to deepen our sense of belonging, strengthen our bonds and also entrench our sense of mutual responsibility and care towards each other.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: One thing that came through strongly from all these conversations was that unity in Singapore's context entails embracing diversity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is not about being the same but being able to engage across all our differences.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And it is also about being stronger than the sum of our parts.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Participants spoke about deepening our shared culture, heritage and experiences.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They spoke of creating opportunities for all of us to interact and connect with one another, and of how the arts and sports are integral in this respect.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They spoke of bringing people across racial, religious and generational lines together, to work on issues that matter to them.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: My colleagues and I will address the various cuts raised by Members speak MCCY's work to strengthen our core identity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They help us deepen our sense of a shared identity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our national cultural institutions, museums, galleries, as well as arts and culture groups offer diverse programmes throughout the year.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In fact, recently, the Peranakan Museum and also the Children's Museum in Singapore reopened and opened their doors with refreshed and interactive exhibits to tell of our Singapore story.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We also continue to celebrate Singapore's intangible cultural heritage and traditional art forms.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These include activities organised by clan associations or arts practitioners which feature dialects as suggested by Mr Dennis Tan.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And as Mr Tan knows, that is already being done.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have performances such as Nanyin and Teochew Opera by Siong Leng Musical Association and Nam Hwa Opera respectively.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is in recognising that Chinese dialects are part of the Singapore Chinese culture and heritage, even as the Government maintains its existing language policy of promoting the use of Mandarin as one of our four official languages.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Government is committed to growing the arts and heritage sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Government funding has held steady in these sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our arts spaces have also grown over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We also continue to support arts and heritage organisations to diversify their income streams via fundraising, with the Cultural Matching Fund and the Sustain the Arts (stART) Fund.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, Ms Tin Pei Ling, Mr Raj Joshua Thomas and Mr Xie Yao Quan asked about our plans for the arts and heritage sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Even during the pandemic, the sectors responded with resolve and enhanced their capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As we emerge from the pandemic, we do want to consolidate the gains that we have made and unlock new opportunities that have come our way.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is thus timely to embark on a journey together with the sectors to envision the future.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Many more provided their feedback online and also during roadshows across the island.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These engagements are important, as we want these two plans to be co-created and co-owned with the arts and heritage communities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Through the process, I met many arts and heritage practitioners.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They shared with me how the arts and heritage sectors in Singapore have, indeed, come a long way, as many Members here have appreciated, and how we can take these sectors, building on the strengths that we have, standing on the shoulders of the giants that have come before us, to take us to the next phase.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan spoke about helping the arts sector grow and develop these new capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have heard from arts practitioners and observed during the pandemic that increasing collaborations between the arts and adjacent industries present many opportunities for Singapore artists.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They can cultivate new audiences and markets and develop new revenue streams.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These measures will help artists and arts groups achieve greater growth and success.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It will help them to deepen their reach to existing audiences and broaden their exposure to new ones.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our plans to grow the creative economy through our arts plan will, in turn, create better job prospects and pathways for our future graduates.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In the next bound, there will be greater focus on increasing access to the arts, creating more occasions for people to share meaningful experiences through the arts.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And we will do this by adopting a data-driven approach to better understand the needs and preferences of audiences and also by expanding partnerships to increase touchpoints.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will also leverage technology and innovation to expand the playing field for the arts.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: My colleague, Minister of State Low Yen Ling, will elaborate further on Our SG Arts Plan when she speaks.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: On arts spaces, we agree with Mr Darryl David that spaces for the arts are crucial in the arts ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Government has, in fact, been very deliberate in developing spaces for the arts, ensuring that they are used optimally and efficiently; that there is also fair access and inclusive opportunities, especially for new groups and younger practitioners.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We now have a diverse range of arts spaces.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Artists can collaborate with one another at multi-tenanted arts housing spaces managed by NAC.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: MCCY and NAC also facilitate arts groups to take up direct leases on state properties and in commercial developments.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In developing arts spaces, we engage closely with the arts community and also work to co-create spaces and think of ideas on how to use these spaces with members of the community.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have been working closely with the arts community, for example, to develop 45 Armenian Street.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We set up a resource panel, and the resource panel comprises private arts practitioners: an actor, an independent music producer, arts academics and also a former chair of the Substation, to give their views, discuss ideas, think about what the 45 Armenian Street might look like.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our shared goal, to ensure that the space will remain an inclusive one that supports artistic experimentation and development of young practitioners.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have received the Resource Panel's recommendations, and NAC will build upon these recommendations to guide the development and design for 45 Armenian Street.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Another example is Kampong Java, another space that I have spoken about previously.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin asked about our plans to safeguard our National Monuments.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I had announced in 2021 that we will be restoring the Istana main building and the former Istana Kampong Gelam.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Istana has featured prominently in Singapore's transition from colony to sovereign state, and the upcoming restoration works will ensure that it will remain well-preserved and functional for its historical importance and as a venue for important state functions and community events.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The former Istana Kampong Gelam, which houses the Malay Heritage Centre (MHC), has also closed for restoration and a gallery revamp, following the MHC Closing Fest last year.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Two other National Monuments housing the National Museum of Singapore, and the Sun Yat Sen Nanyang Memorial Hall, are also scheduled for restoration.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In addition to preserving our places, we have enriched the Singapore story also with treasures in our National Collection.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Beyond physical objects and buildings, we have safeguarded and showcased our intangible cultural heritage.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have also deepened our collaboration with Singaporeans through co-created exhibitions and programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Hazmi Zin from Rumah Makan Minang, for instance, was one of 45 business owners who participated in the Kampong Gelam Citizen Engagement Project and his participation, along with others, has enriched our understanding of the precinct's cultural heritage.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For the second edition of Our SG Heritage Plan, we will make a bigger push to reflect a more layered understanding of the Singapore identity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Design, such as fashion, craft and architecture, is an important expression of our cultural identity and a catalyst for creativity and innovation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We also hope to strengthen the ties between our museums and the design community and industry.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: NHB will, therefore, explore new ways for Singaporeans to get involved in presenting and sharing our heritage with others.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will also support the heritage sector by using technology, and Minister of State Low Yen Ling will elaborate on this plan when she speaks.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And we want to optimise our sporting facilities and spaces to encourage more people to come together, socialise, play together.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This will ensure a stronger alignment between what the Government aims to achieve and the key performance indicators (KPIs) that KASM will have to aspire towards.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Darryl David and Mr Xie Yao Quan also asked about the developments following the takeover and our plans ahead.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Under the new management team, we have had many activities in the past three months alone.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And we took over on 9 December last year, so, just about three months.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These events and activities include performances by live bands and dance groups as well as community events, such as the FunFam SportFest, a Big Walk event to usher in the New Year, and a Chinese New Year Stadium Waterfront Carnival.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Last weekend, I just at the Sports Hub, and I saw many casual joggers, kids with their families playing football and playing basketball.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It rained a lot, but we could use the promenade – an area around the 100Plus track – to great effect.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Student-athletes have also been participating in the National School Games at the Sports Hub, competing hard, both at the National Stadium, as well as at the covered courts in the Sports Hub.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In the coming months, members of the public can look forward to more of such activities, including some National School Games finals, the National Stadium Open Houses, as well as grassroots events.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I want to assure him that we will also be stepping up on our communication efforts by leveraging social media, word-of-mouth, engaging our partners, work with more broadcasters to bring more Singaporeans to the Sports Hub, by raising awareness of the events and activities that we will have at the Sports Hub.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At the same time, concerts and marquee sports events have also experienced an upswing also in the same period of time.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: A few weeks ago, we hosted Westlife, which sold out for three consecutive nights.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This was notwithstanding that, on one of the nights, the Red Hot Chilli Peppers' were competing for eyeballs just across the road at the National Stadium.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Both were sold out, both happened on a weekday night, no less.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We also have FIBA, which is the International Basketball Association, which will be having its Intercontinental Cup in Singapore for the very first time.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And we, certainly, hope that Mr Mark Chay would not find that it will remain a ghost town for much longer.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: With these developments, we will move towards using more of the whole Kallang Alive Precinct in synergy, to offer a greater array of international sporting events, alongside local programming.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For instance, we can combine the facilities at the OCBC Arena, Singapore Indoor Stadium and the new Kallang Tennis Centre, and be able to confidently bring in marquee sporting events, such as, for example, an ATP1000 sporting event.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In parallel, Singaporeans in the community can try out the sport at the community level, at community tennis sessions, for example, or tennis clinics for social competitive players and aspiring athletes, youth competitions and so on, activating the entire precinct, not just the Sports Hub, but the broader precinct that is Kallang Alive.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So we will have a whole ecosystem of sports across a diverse range of sporting levels, all integrated with the other upcoming lifestyle and entertainment offerings.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For our national teams, let me assure Mr Mark Chay that the NSAs continue to be prioritised in the booking of Sports Hub and ActiveSG facilities for national team trainings.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In fact, with the Government now taking charge of the Sports Hub facilities, we can better optimise the use of these facilities across various uses.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, to give Mr Mark Chay one example, SportSG worked with Singapore Gymnastics to ensure that our gymnasts could train at Sengkang Sports Hall, while their usual training venue at OCBC Arena Hall was activated to host the Singapore International Rhythmic Gymnastics Cup.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, we have one international gymnastics event at the usual training centre but, at the same time, we could use other spaces within our facilities across the island to continue the tempo of national training unabated.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Even during, or perhaps, in particular, during the COVID-19 pandemic period, this continued to rise to 74% in 2022, which are all very encouraging signs.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These indicators show that more Singaporeans are keen to get more active.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In addition to the sport events at the Sports Hub that I shared earlier, the public also enjoy sporting activities across Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In 2022, 148 community leagues and competitions were organised across 19 ActiveSG Sport Centres and bear in mind that for 2022, or part of that period at least, we were not able to come out and do these events.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But once we were able to, we had more than a hundred of such events and leagues going on at the 19 ActiveSG Centres across Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This involved more than 13,000 participants, including young children and seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Last year, we introduced the ActiveSG Cup which saw more than 1,300 participants across two sports – Basketball and Football.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This will apply to all who are ActiveSG members or sign up as new members between 1 May and 31 October this year.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Parents may use these credits to offset the cost of their children's ActiveSG programmes and cover their entry fees into ActiveSG facilities, such as our swimming pools.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This, I hope, will encourage more children to play together with their peers, with their neighbours and their families outside of structured school sport participation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are working hard to build more and better sporting facilities throughout Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will enhance access and also step up on having a greater variety of programming at these facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our hope is that every Singaporean will have ample opportunity to enjoy, engage and excel in sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: To Mr Sharael Taha and Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap's questions on developing Singapore football, and I get this every year at every Committee of Supply, we launched Unleash the Roar!

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: (UTR) in 2021 to develop a strong local pipeline of football talents.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This was intended to be and it is a long-term plan that we have put in place to grow the base of participation, to identify talented players from a young age and provide these talented players with rigorous training and structured opportunities to be coached well, to compete regularly and to have a clear pathway to the national team.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will expand the number of SFAs and also increase the programme intake over the year.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These SFAs, together with the Singapore Sports School, the ActiveSG Football Academy as well as all private clubs and academies in Singapore, provide a broad base of participation for us to identify suitable talents.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will put in place a national framework to systematically select and develop the best players from this broad base.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our best young footballers aged 13 to 17 will be drawn from all our available pipelines that I described earlier to these squads.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This centre will be our primary pathway for selection to our national team.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Within this centre, players will be selected into core and also reserve teams, and we will review them periodically.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Because we do not want anyone to be too comfortable or too complacent and we want to ensure that throughout the squads, across the different age groups, there will be competitive tension.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These boys and girls will train and compete regularly as a team.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are looking at setting up a youth league that will give our players regular opportunities to be competing at high levels.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They will also, from time to time, come together, to train as a squad, so that they can get to know each other, train and play together, and on occasion, also compete overseas for even further exposure.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These players will also be supported with a comprehensive suite of sport science, nutrition and sports medicine.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Second, I think Mr Faisal Manap and Mr Sharael Taha, raised these points on talent identification and scouting.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have a small population with a small base and we need to ensure that we have our eyes on all available talent all the time.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will progressively roll out training on talent identification for coaches and strengthen our scouts' capabilities in identifying the best of our young footballers.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We also want to tap on the experience of our ex-national players, our ex-national coaches, who already have an eye for talent, having taken part at the highest level of the game.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will invite them to be trained and to be part of our scouting network.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: To ensure consistency in our training and development ecosystem, a common coaching syllabus is already being used, across all the SFAs and the national youth squads.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: More than 500 coaches and teachers have already been trained with this curriculum to date.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will also introduce coaching licensing and renewal after coaches have acquired the necessary Continuing Coach Education hours.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will also find suitable opportunities for our coaches to learn from the best, to be immersed in the environment, so that they can have an experience of what it is like to be coaching at the highest levels.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For example, our partnership with Spanish LaLiga has allowed us to bring in experienced youth coaches from Spain to augment our local coaches, as well as provide overseas learning opportunities for them.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At the same time, similar local scholarships will also be available for suitable footballers who choose to enrol in the Singapore Sports School.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Through this, we hope to prepare them for future overseas scholarship programmes and opportunities, and also spur more footballers to be enrolled in a full-time programme for their football development.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: More details of the scholarship will be shared when ready.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Eligible footballers can tap on existing support avenues to continue training and competing, whilst at the same time, fulfilling NS obligations.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Developing talent takes time and our focus is really on laying a strong foundation for long-term growth and learning.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are putting in place a systematic infrastructure to expand, to nurture and to develop this pool of young players at the base level, starting from when they are 13.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The best will be identified and put into a national development centre, as I have outlined.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They will play and compete and train regularly, both locally as well as overseas.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Over time, this initiative will provide us with a steady pipeline of players to choose from.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It will take time, and much as I know, all of us are invested in the outcome of Singapore football and I have heard the emotional, passionate speeches made by Members earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I would ask for our continued and all your continued support for this system to ensure that our younger players have a chance to progress and become the pool for future national team selection.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The strength of our cohesive society, in my view, is not found only in what we have in common but also manifests in how we negotiate our differences and deal with conflicts that inevitably arise.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ms Joan Pereira, Miss Cheng Li Hui and Mr Xie Yao Quan asked about enhancements to the Community Dispute Management Framework (CDMF).

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: An inter-agency workgroup, led by MCCY, together with MinLaw and the Ministry of National Development (MND), have been conducting a review of the CDMF.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann and I have already spoken about the enhancements in different areas relevant to MND and MinLaw's COS debates respectively.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: To pull it all together, let me reiterate how we are enhancing this framework.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, we want to promote community norms as our first line of defence.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I think Senior Minister of State Sim Ann made that very clear and I too, reiterated that when I spoke in my MinLaw capacity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Clearer social norms encourage the self-management of behaviours.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As Senior Minister of State Sim Ann said, Municipal Services Office (MSO) has been working with partners to promote community norms for noise management recommended by the Community Advisory Panel on Neighbourhood Noise.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Second, we are looking at allowing dedicated personnel to leverage stronger laws and help these neighbours resolve their issues upstream.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In other words, before it gets to the stage where it becomes intransigent or intractable, and they have to go to the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals (CDRT) or other adjudicatory tribunals to resolve their differences.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For instance, this team will be able to conduct investigations, or direct residents to attend mandatory mediation or to stop the actions that are causing the nuisance pending the mediation or the adjudication.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As Senior Minister of State Sim Ann shared last week, MSO will be piloting this with disputes arising from serious noise disturbances between neighbours.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will also explore consequences for recalcitrant offenders who fail to stop the actions as required.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Third, we will increase access to community mediation and mandate mediation for certain types of disputes between neighbours.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This trend, by and large, has been consistently the case over the past few years.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In other words, they form the bulk of all cases registered for mediation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In many cases, clear expectations on acceptable community behaviours as well as a mutual appreciation of what the parties are facing would go a long way towards improving the situation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Hence, we want to encourage disputing neighbours to find an amicable, mediated settlement of their disputes as far as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This we have to do, because with all these steps that we take, by the time a case ends up at the CDRT, there would have been numerous attempts at mediation, at reconciliation, and these probably represent the most intractable and intransigent of cases.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We want an effective and efficient, speedy framework to deal with these problems.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Those steps are what I had elaborated upon when I spoke at the MinLaw Commitee of Supply.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Even strengthen the teeth on mediation and CDRT, and we mandate mediation, let me emphasise: even as we are looking at leveraging stronger laws, these should not be used as a first recourse.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We interact with our neighbours on a daily basis.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Most of us want to live peacefully side by side with our neighbours.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: When disputes arise and intervention is needed, we encourage disputing neighbours to go through mediation as far as possible, allowing parties to talk to each other about the issues that vex them and through the assistance of trained and oftentimes, very effective mediators, find a common path.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We need the diverse strengths and talents from the community to tackle the challenges we face as a nation and build Singapore's future together.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our youths play a crucial role in this regard.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Youths today are well informed, more prepared, more ready and they want to engage with us to discuss policies.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling spoke about engaging youths.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: MCCY and the National Youth Council (NYC) have continued to engage and partner with youths on national issues in different ways.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These include policy co-creation platforms such as the Youth Circles and programmes such as the Youth Action Challenge that supports them, not just in talking about these ideas or listening to the suggestions, but in working with them actively to turn their ideas into action.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: From our ForwardSG engagements, we continue to see a very healthy, sustained youth interest in policy-making and want to create more opportunities to meet these aspirations.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, MCCY and NYC, are exploring ways to create more policy space, and also work on how to institutionalise involvement of more youths in policy-making and elevate their proposals for consideration onto a national platform.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will share more details when this is ready.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling asked about our plans to expand our youth leadership programmes to provide younger student leaders the opportunity to engage on national issues and build strong networks.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: NYC and the National Community Leadership Institute (NACLI), in partnership with MOE, piloted the inaugural Our Singapore Leadership Programme (OSLP) last year.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This was a programme, as a pilot, for about 50 Secondary 4 students from MOE schools and madrasahs.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: All the student leaders who participated in the inaugural OSLP came from different shools.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In other words, we had about 53 students from 53 different schools. "Leader" is defined broadly.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Some were head of student councils; some were participants in their dance groups, and others, captains of their sports teams or members of the uniformed groups.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They came together to reflect on and discuss issues which confront Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They talked about and grappled with trade-offs and the complexities of policy-designs; and they expanded their network of friends, people they can talk to, connections that they can make and forge new friendships.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We found this programme very successful, and we want to give more youths an opportunity to take part in this programme.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For students from the institutes of higher learning, NYC will develop a new leadership programme.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan has pointed out, and I agree with him, that there is value in having and promoting active citizenry, volunteerism and collaboration.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And these traits must continue to underpin our society and our social compact.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will resource them better, so that they in turn can support the various social service agencies that are under their watch and they are working with, so they can better channel volunteers and donations-in-kind to meet unmet needs.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will also support businesses in their efforts to be a force for good for society as they design their business practices and operations in ways that benefit their employees, their stakeholders, and, of course, the wider community that they serve.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Minister of State Alvin Tan will share more details when he speaks.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Don Wee asked how our Self-help Groups (SHGs) are collaborating to enhance outcomes across ethnic communities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: While the SHGs were set up to provide customised support for their respective ethnic communities, they also work together and strengthen mutual support across the different ethnic communities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These efforts by our SHGs embody the Singapore Together spirit – Singaporeans, diverse as we may be, stepping forward, working together and building a better nation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Chairman, to conclude, I have spoken about our various MCCY initiatives – and my colleagues that follow will elaborate on many of these and speak of various other measures as well.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But our principal focus is to deepen our roots and expand the reach of our arts and heritage.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We do not do that just as an end in itself, but as a means to an end, to promote arts, culture and heritage, sporting participation and excellence, both at the community and at a professional level.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We do this to foster neighbourliness, care and active citizenry, as part of the unique our Singaporean DNA.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These efforts speak to what it means to call Singapore our home.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our home is not just a physical space.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is also how we see ourselves, all of us, as connected and bound to others in Singapore through arts, heritage, culture, sports and religion.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is about who we are as a people, our shared experiences, what we do to care for each other and look out for one another and the values we hold dear and live by.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These are the threads that bind us and hold our social compact together.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These are the threads that run through each of us as Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Growing these aspects of Singapore is delicate work, but it is important and it requires the commitment of all of us, regardless of language, race, religion and social-economic background.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Minister, I would like to extend my condolences.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I know it is not easy after last night's development to talk about football.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Last month, I joined 80 of our will Woodgrove residents and their children to visit the museum where we spent an enjoyable afternoon together partaking in activities, such as travelling back in time to the olden Singapore to experience life as our forefathers had and learning how various communities in Singapore celebrate birthdays.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: (In Mandarin)   Mr Chairman, to promote local arts and culture, arts and cultural practitioners are indispensable.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: During the pandemic, they have faced severe challenges.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Most of them are self-employed, without the support of an organisation.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: They would inevitably be hit hard by the economic downturn.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: How would the Government revitalise and develop the local arts and culture ecosystem, and empower our arts and cultural practitioners?

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: In addition to our plans to build a thriving arts and heritage sector in Singapore, there are essentially two ingredients that will go a long way to help achieve the objectives set out in the plans.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: First, it is to ensure that there is adequate infrastructure or arts spaces which will not only add much vibrancy to the sector, but more importantly, support both our arts and heritage practitioners and create opportunities for Singaporeans to come together.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: The Minister gave the example of 45 Armenian Street.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Minister of State Low Yen Ling also shared about the Singapore Art Museum at Tanjong Pagar Distripark and the developing arts and culture sandboxes at Kampong Java.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Such art spaces are important as they are key enablers in the overall ecosystem and support a diverse set of multi-disciplinary practitioners in their respective areas of practice.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: I therefore invite the Minister to share more about MCCY's plans to add, update and diversify our arts spaces in order to support the arts and heritage sector.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Next, investments in the arts and heritage sector's capabilities are crucial in developing a globally relevant and resilient ecosystem and workforce, which will drive our creative economy.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: At the last MCCY COS debate, it was shared that there will be a strong drive towards digitalisation and the harnessing of digital technologies in order to create new opportunities for the sector.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: The Arts and Culture Digital Roadmap was launched early last year to support arts and culture stakeholders and practitioners in assessing their own digital readiness and learn of possible solutions and opportunities available to support their work.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Self-employed persons (SEPs) form a core segment of the talent in our arts and culture landscape.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: However, in order for them to thrive in and contribute to the sector, there is a need to ensure that they have adequate support in order to continually build on their skills and also improve their working conditions.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Minister of State Low Yen Ling announced at the COS debate last year that the National Arts Council (NAC) would increase opportunities for capacity development of SEPs, work with industry partners to better ensure protection and working conditions for SEPs and pilot new ways for SEPs to create new value in the arts sector and beyond.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: I therefore invite the Minister to share MCCY's plans to build on the capabilities of our arts and heritage practitioners, as well as its efforts to strengthen the entire ecosystem; and further, to also share what kind of further assistance will be offered to SEPs to support employability and help them build a sustainable career in the arts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, our arts and heritage are central to our Singapore identity and bring us together as one people.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The resumption of various physical events and large-scale gatherings will allow MCCY to make further strides towards shaping a bold and resilient arts and culture sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We seek to achieve this in close partnership with the arts community and fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In the past year, I have engaged with our practitioners and fellow Singaporeans to hear and learn more about their aspirations for Singapore's arts and heritage scene.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: One of the common themes to emerge is the wish for an inclusive and forward-looking landscape where our arts and culture can continue to grow and flourish.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, Mr Xie Yao Quan, Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Raj Joshua Thomas – they have all asked about our plans for the arts and heritage sector moving forward.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The stART Fund also supported Legend: The Beginnings (传说之 人之初), which brought the art of Chinese orchestra to our audiences by retelling Chinese folklore through an immersive experience that combines music with story narration and animation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To grow our audiences, we supported and delivered a range of programmes like Arts in Your Neighbourhood and Silver Arts, which brought arts experience to neighbourhoods and older Singaporeans, as mentioned passionately by many Members earlier during their speeches.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We also launched initiatives like the Arts x Tech Lab in 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This has fostered, especially during COVID-19, vibrant collaboration between the arts and tech sectors for innovative experimentation, and also deepened the arts industry’s digital capabilities in art-making and presentation of arts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will better leverage technology and the use of data to catalyse new possibilities for our practitioners, for our arts organisations and fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will widen our base of partners as MCCY works closely with the arts and culture sector to shape a bright and exciting arts and culture scene.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We envision the arts linking our society across all key aspects of our life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas asked about our plans to develop spaces for communities to connect with one another.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I want to assure him we will expand touchpoints for the arts by offering more arts activities in parks, in community and lifestyle spaces which are readily accessible.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To complement this, NAC will support research efforts to grow evidence on the social impact of the arts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Ms Hany Soh spoke about the importance of creating opportunities for our young to learn and pursue their passion for the arts, and we agree with her.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC, National Heritage Board (NHB) and our cultural institutions currently offer a wide range of arts and heritage events and programmes for families with young children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: These include National Gallery Singapore (NGS)'s Children's Biennale, NHB's Children's Season, as well as initiatives via NAC’s arts and culture nodes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC's funding towards major art companies also supports outreach efforts to children, such as the Singapore Repertory Theatre's division called The Little Company.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We encourage parents to enrich their family life by supporting and by participating in all these initiatives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will also deepen our collaboration with the Ministry of Education (MOE) on the Museum-Based Learning and Arts Education Programme, to provide our students with hands-on experiences as they learn about Singapore's arts and heritage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We aim to develop Singapore into a distinctive city with accessible spaces and precincts for our people to enjoy the arts where they live, work and play.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This ongoing effort will bring Government agencies and private stakeholders together to grow vibrant precincts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC, too, will aim to grow a flourishing and globally-connected creative economy for the arts, as mentioned by Minister Edwin Tong, through new business models, development pathways and internationalisation opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It will also continue to support local arts practitioners so that they can reach international audiences and gain recognition overseas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I will elaborate on some of these initiatives later in my speech.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Chairman, our Singapore heritage is a unique one that we are proud of.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will launch Our SG Heritage Plan 2.0 this year and build upon the progress we have achieved so far.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Today, our Hawker Culture is inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the ICH of Humanity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have established The Stewards of ICH Awards to recognise excellent practitioners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Besides three new community galleries, we also piloted the Street Corner Heritage Galleries in Balestier, Kampong Gelam, Little India and Chinatown.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In recent years, the Padang, Fort Siloso and three Singapore River bridges were gazetted as National Monuments to preserve locations of significant history.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Under identity, we will find new ways to reflect the many layers of our Singapore story and its connections with the rest of the world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Apart from efforts, in the area of archaeology, we will encourage content-based and object contributions from the public and offer more opportunities for Singaporeans to co-create exhibitions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Moving forward, NHB will work with other agencies, including Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) and National Library Board (NLB), to collect works of contemporary Singaporean designers and architects and, potentially, from the region.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We can all look forward to an upcoming exhibition on the works of Andrew Gn.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: He is one of Singapore's most prolific fashion designers – at the Asian Civilisations Museum (ACM) later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: At the community level, we will work with Singaporeans from all walks of life to co-create more heritage touchpoints, like holding festivals and organising cultural programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In particular, we hope to have more youths join us, like volunteer Mr Ng Wee Liang, who helped to document heritage businesses as part of NHB’s Kampong Gelam Citizen Engagement Project.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As part of Our SG Arts and Heritage Plans, we will continue to bring arts and heritage closer to fellow Singaporeans and in our everyday environment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will work with citizens and agencies to introduce public artworks and co-develop heritage programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin and Mr Darryl David had asked about our plans to update our arts spaces to better support our practitioners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We remain committed to developing user-centric and inclusive arts spaces, particularly for emerging arts groups and practitioners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Last year I shared about NAC and Singapore Land Authority (SLA)'s plans to refurbish and pilot arts and culture sandboxes at Kampong Java.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: After NAC's focus group discussions with key stakeholders, it was agreed that Kampong Java should be a sandbox and multidisciplinary venue for artists to experience and incubate works of different art forms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It should also remain an accessible and affordable space for artists.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The pandemic has spurred digital innovations which have brought new opportunities and wider audiences to the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As part of Our SG Arts and Heritage Plans, NAC and NHB will introduce various digital initiatives to transform the way we enjoy and learn about our arts and heritage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Later this month, NAC will launch a beta version of a one-stop digital platform for audiences to discover, to share and to book arts and culture events.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This platform will also help cultivate and deepen interest in the arts amongst Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As a start, it will feature arts and culture events in the museums under NHB, the National Gallery Singapore and Esplanade, and offer users personalised recommendations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: More features will be rolled out progressively over the year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Further, we will work closely with our practitioners as well as private stakeholders to further drive the adoption of digital technologies and solutions across the arts and heritage sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For example, NAC will work with UOB on the UOBNAC Acceleration Programme for the Arts, which seeks to help artists and organisations build on their business and financial competencies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC will continue to organise the next edition of "Arts Matters" this year, which aims to facilitate interdisciplinary and cross-sector learning with technology and commercial partners, such as Branded.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC will leverage the Metaverse to showcase Singapore as a distinctive city for the arts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: As more opportunities in the metaverse are unlocked, there is new potential for audience development, for monetisation and for the growth of innovative technologies for the arts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, NHB will partner the private sector to explore the development of new digital strategies for the heritage sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This will include ways to digitally preserve and document our heritage assets, and how to augment visitor experiences at the museums through Virtual Reality experiences, 3D displays and artificial intelligence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We are looking forward to harnessing technology to create new experiences and enhance our appreciation of arts and culture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Apart from leveraging new platforms, MCCY will deepen investments in our people.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I agree with Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Sitoh Yih Pin that we must develop the capabilities of our workforce and the resources needed for a thriving creative economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC will also be collaborating with our Institutes of Higher Learning and continuing education and training centres to strengthen career pathways in the arts and culture sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This includes embedding digital skills as part of the students’ Pre-Employment Training (PET), and curating resources to support the organisational processes and transformation of our arts groups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It currently oversees three co-working and performance spaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It will embark on a series of deep dive sessions with various arts SEPs to gain insights and their feedback on the development of the ARH and aim to enhance the hub progressively this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This follows my meeting last month with a group of more than 30 arts SEPs during which we discussed how we can better support them and co-create solutions together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, I would like to extend my gratitude to every one who came forward to share their hopes for our arts and culture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Together, we have carved a vision of an inclusive, accessible and vibrant arts and heritage sector that will anchor and inspire Singaporeans for years to come.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MCCY is committed to partner our practitioners and Singaporeans to realise this collective vision for a distinctive, connected and creative Singapore.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I, and I am sure that other Singapore youth as well, will be very interested to hear from the Ministry on what are the upcoming developments of Somerset Belt and the programmes that we can look forward to.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Xie Yao Quan, you can take both cuts together.

text: During the COVID-19 period, we saw many religious organisations come together and partnering with the local community with a common purpose of serve the helpless and the vulnerable in the neighbourhood.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Take, for example, the Church of St Anthony (CSA) in Woodgrove.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: For the past two years, CSA has been partnering with Woodgrove Division through the People's Association (PA) to organise Harvest of Love events at least twice a year where the parishers and our grassroots volunteers would distribute care packs to low-income residents.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Recently, the Harvest of Love initiative took place within the Church where low-income families of all races and religions were invited to have lunch at the Church with choir performances and presented with festive rations, care packs thereafter.

text: What role can the Harmony Circle play to encourage more of such ground-up initiatives —

text: Chairman, Outward Bound School (OBS) has been a significant and memorable experience for many Singaporeans growing up.

text: It teaches great resilience and courage to step out of one's comfort zone and it brings students from different schools together.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: I am glad that OBS programmes have resumed, post-COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Can the Ministry provide an update on its progress and share its plans for how many circles in the year ahead?

text: Chairman, Singapore is a multi-racial and multi-religious society.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Our unity in such diversity is something we have worked hard to achieve and have been working hard to improve.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Racial and religious harmony is the lynchpin of our vibrant and rich Singapore culture.

text: Last year, MCCY announced that that the IRCC would be renamed as the Racial and Religious Harmony Circles.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: The new Harmony Circles will serve as a platform to promote racial and religious harmony here, with presence in every Constituency.

text: Mental health conditions at times manifest themselves less than physical ones.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: For this reason, they are harder to detect and can be difficult to treat.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Mental health patients have traditionally also suffered more stigma.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: While we have seen increasing support for mental health, we should also strive towards its equability.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: We have all known, seen or heard of people hard labouring under mental health conditions.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: However, there perhaps remains some whose conditions are not known to themselves or others.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Chairman, no one should ever have to suffer alone.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Can MCCY share what initiatives there have been and will be rolled out the SG Mental Well-Being Network?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Mr Chairman, the Budget has provided assurance, especially to lower-income Singaporeans who are already living close to the edge of their financial capabilities.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: While we ensure that Singaporeans' physical well-being is taken care of, we must not neglect their mental well-being.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As physical and mental health are intertwined, there can still be targeted support measures and platforms to prioritise mental well-being.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As such, there are three questions I would like to raise to MCCY.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: First, the launch of SG Mental Well-Being Network in July 2022 is a testament of ongoing efforts in increasing mental health literacy, awareness and serves as a platform for others seeking appropriate resources.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Could MCCY provide an update on the progress of the SG Mental Well-Being Network?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
