speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Mr Chairman, as a business owner and entrepreneur, I believe in giving back to the community.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: In many sport-forward countries, businesses adopt sports organisations or teams.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: In return, the companies increase their brand awareness and get access to athletes and coaches for their organisation and staff development.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Therefore, I request that MCCY provide information on how it motivates enterprises to participate in charitable causes, such as volunteering or donating to our community and charities.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: Caring for our vulnerable is a whole-of-society effort and I am encouraged to see many corporates do their part in this area.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: Another towkay shared that given the manpower crunch faced by many SMEs now, volunteering time could be something that is challenging.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: Can the Ministry provide an update on how the BIPS uptake has been and how the Ministry may promote and share the programme better.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: Can the scheme also be expanded to include other forms of support that a corporation can make?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: The Alliance for Action (Afa) on Corporate Purpose rallies Singapore's business leaders and corporations to combine their resources and to serve community needs and realise our vision of a caring and inclusive society.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: The corporate sector is a critical force for good.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: It can uplift the communities that they operate in, protect employee well-being, promote ethical supplier partnerships and ensure environmental sustainability.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: For example, in Punggol, our local supermarkets sell at cost, organic vegetables from our volunteer farms, work with the NTUC on fair workplaces practices, promote plastic recycling with our cleaning vendors and contribute essentials to our vulnerable families.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: Indeed, we need more purpose-driven businesses in our communities.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: They can anchor much goodness in our neighbourhoods.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: I ask the Ministry to give an update to the Afa.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: What are the Ministry's plans to encourage the growth of purpose driven business entities and how will the Ministry support our businesses to better give back to the communities they serve?

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Chairman, we are building ecosystems for impact together with our community, our corporates and our youths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It is doing so in the following ways.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: First, it is helping remove the stigma for individuals to seek help.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Last year, some members of this House and I shared our past struggles in a YouTube video called "99 Singaporeans sharing their darkest moments".

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This was one of the Network's contributions to a series of initiatives for World Mental Health Day 2022, which aimed to rally people to build a caring society for everyone, particularly those who are struggling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Second, the Network has started regular Partners' Networking Sessions to share ideas and aspirations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These Circles strengthen community and peer support by equipping volunteers with the skills to care for themselves and also for others.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Last week, I met Mr Kenny Sng, who is leading efforts to ensure grassroot volunteers can recognise and support those with mental health conditions in Bukit Batok East.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: He shared that his Well-being Circle is a key platform for his volunteers and leaders to collaborate with partners, such as the Singapore Anglican Community Services, Club Heal and the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC).

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Over the next year, Kenny, along with 400 other trained volunteers and around 30 partners from other Mental Well-Being Circles, will continue to serve their communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will learn from these Circles and then scale up our efforts in other locations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Similarly, our Racial and Religious Harmony Circles, previously known as IRCCs, have strengthened ties and built trust among our ethnic and religious communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui, Ms Hany Soh and Mr Xie Yao Quan asked about the progress and plans of our Harmony Circles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: A key part of our refresh is to help Harmony Circles digitalise and diversify their composition, so they continue to be relevant and effective at fostering harmony within our communities and we have a few encouraging examples.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Encik Fazlur Rahman leads Kembangan-Chai Chee's Harmony Circle.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: He was actively involved in our IRCC Refresh Workgroup last year and he is working to make his Harmony Circle more digital and more diverse.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Eunos Harmony Circle leaders, Nazath Faheema and Benjamin Tan, are recruiting youths and equipping digital skills into their Harmony Circle.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They recently used social media to urge their communities and the public to stay united following reports that several youths had been radicalised online.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We hope more Harmony Circles will follow in their footsteps.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Next month, more youths, females and representatives from other religious and community organisations will start their new term as Harmony Circle leaders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They will receive training on mediation, interfaith and digital media.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: If you are a religious organisation or an individual passionate about interfaith and inter-racial work, please join our Harmony Circles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will also dedicate July as our Racial and Religious Harmony Month from this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Apart from celebrating Racial Harmony Day on 21 July, our Harmony Circles and other community partners will organise activities throughout July to celebrate and promote racial and religious harmony.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Community initiatives, like our Mental Well-Being and Harmony Circles, need volunteers and coordination.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Mark Chay, Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Mohamad Fahmi and Mr Xie Yao Quan asked how our SG Cares movement can make volunteering more sustainable and effective.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: SG Cares Volunteer Centres coordinate efforts to channel volunteers and donations-in-kind to unmet local needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This means our Volunteer Centres have engaged 45,000 volunteers and served 340,000 beneficiaries in the past year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are working with the National Council of Social Service (NCSS) and Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS) to strengthen our Volunteer Centres, to help them better equip their community partners with capabilities in volunteer management, training, partnerships, digitalisation and communications.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are also encouraging more professionals to contribute their skills and expertise, by engaging SG Cares National Intermediaries, across the legal, accounting, engineering and chartered secretaries sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Individuals, schools, and corporates who wish to volunteer your time and talents, please find out more at nearest Volunteer Centre on our SG Cares website.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Just as our communities are coming together for impact, our corporates are also stepping up.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The median percentage of employee volunteering has increased from 25% in 2017 to 50% in 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling asked about the take-up and plans of the Corporate Volunteer Scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: From 2016 to 2021, businesses made 164 claims and took up about 4,700 volunteering opportunities under this scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: When I met Q&M Dental CEO Dr Ng Chin Siau two weeks ago, he shared how his Cares Committee has launched multiple community projects, including working closely with People’s Association to set up free dental clinics for the underprivileged.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In line with this blueprint, NVPC has also refreshed its Company of Good programme for companies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Edward Chia will be pleased to know that the programme will include aspects of employee well-being and that we are exploring how more businesses can adopt our blueprint’s goals with partners such as Enterprise Singapore and the Singapore Business Federation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We have also enhanced the Corporate Volunteer Scheme, including expanding the scope of the scheme's qualifying volunteering activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We hope that this improves adoption of the scheme and strengthens partnerships between corporates and Institutions of a Public Character.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Last December, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and I launched the Mentoring SG movement, which builds upon our Mentoring Alliance for Action (AfA).

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: If you are a company leader, you can one, offer job tasters through the National Youth Council; encourage your employees to sign up as mentors on mentoringsg.com, and partner our Mentoring SG Office to contribute to our mentoring community, offer your venue spaces, amplification channels, and also other expertise.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: (In Mandarin):   As the saying goes, what is taken from the community is given back to the society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: While pursuing business interests, businesses should also proactively undertake social responsibility to co-create a harmonious sustainable society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Businesses can benefit from adopting more purpose-driven models and establishing the culture of mentoring.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example, more consumers are choosing to support businesses that generate value for the wider community, including their suppliers and workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Staff, on the other hand, become more motivated, productive and stay longer with their companies when they know that their company is making an impact on society and investing in their growth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This is especially when senior staff care and look out for their younger colleagues as part of the company's mentoring culture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We recognise that it is not always easy to shift existing business practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: But we have seen how many different businesses have risen to the occasion to become purpose-driven and contribute back to society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: More importantly, businesses do not have to do it alone.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We encourage more companies, including SMEs, to convene, to discuss how to contribute more, collaborate with the Mentoring SG Office or work with the trade and clan associations in developing your initiatives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: (In English): In addition to efforts by our community and corporates, our youths are also playing their part.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Please let me elaborate how we are helping them to do so, in Malay.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: (In Malay):   Throughout the pandemic, our youths were confined to their homes during key life stages such as their schooling years, or when they first joined the workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It also caused many to lose opportunities to gather in person and experience the outdoors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As such, we will renew our urban and natural spaces such as Somerset Belt and OBS@Coney to provide youths with more opportunities to gain important experiences, grow their networks and take on leadership roles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This also complements our youth leadership programmes organised by NYC, such as the Our Singapore Leadership Programme which has been expanded to include younger youth leaders from MOE schools and Madrasahs, that Minister Edwin Tong spoke about.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: (In English): Our youths need space and programmes to do their thing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: At last year's COS, I shared how we have been gathering ideas from youths to transform our Somerset Belt to support their ground-up initiatives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Through our Realise Your Somerset Project (RYSP), we have supported 24 projects and reached out to more than 18,000 youths across different causes in 2022.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Recently, I caught up with Arthur Choo, whose RYSP project, Green Arena, promotes sustainable arts by building drums with repurposed materials.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Green Arena has held virtual sessions and physical art installations and workshops at the Somerset Belt.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Participants from Season 1 of the RYSP also returned as facilitators and co-creators at the workshops, sharing their experiences with latter cohorts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Baey Yam Keng asked for an update on the physical development of our Somerset Belt.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This year, our youths will take greater ownership of the precinct and get to decide how it would look like, operate and also develop future programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Youths keen to shape this space and programmes, at our Somerset Belt can check out our Youth Action Plan website for more details soon.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Moving beyond urban spaces, we are also creating opportunities for our youths to experience the outdoors together again.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Many of us have been through an Outward Bound Singapore (OBS) programme many, many years ago.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: These outdoor adventure education, OAE programmes, build confidence and resilience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It also brings people of diverse backgrounds together, forging friendships while overcoming challenging outdoor activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Last month, I visited our OBS campus and joined students from Dunearn Secondary School, School of the Arts and Westwood Secondary School in their land and sea activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The students were tanned, sunburned, exhausted but had great attitude!

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This Council will strengthen our OAE sector and support the development of safe outdoor activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Since its inception, the Council has started work in three key areas: Standards and Certification, Professional Development, and Safety and Compliance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This year, it will start developing a national OAE standards and certification scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It will also institute a risk assessment and management system to strengthen safety culture across the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, during my recent visit to OBS, I climbed the 20 meter Inverse Tower.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It is taller than the 20 meters suggests.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: While I appeared confident on the outside, in fact, I was, very nervous!

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: My climbing buddy and belayers, Xara and Nadia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Their support and encouragement enabled me to climb the tower.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Leaving Pulau Ubin inspired by our youths, I hope our community partners and purpose-driven businesses will also inspire our youths to become community and corporate leaders and make their mark in our renewed youth spaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Like how Xara, Nadia and I conquered the Inverse Tower as a team, I believe that when different groups of our society join our unique strengths together, we can play our part to move Singapore forward, and upward together.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Mark Chay, you can take your four cuts together.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Additionally, mental health and resilience are essential factors in success in sports.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Lastly, we must recognise the critical role of National Sports Associations and Sports Scientists in continuing to nurture future generations of Olympic hopefuls.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: It cannot be gainsaid that sports can bring about positive change.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: The Olympic spirit has long been associated with camaraderie, excellence and altruism.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: And many athletes have used their privilege and status as a platform for lasting social change.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Our athletes strive to be the best on the field, on the court, in the pool, and use their platforms to do good in society.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Last year at the COS, TeamSG Cares was unveiled – a project which allows present and former athletes to give back to those in need or start charitable initiatives for causes close to their hearts.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: I am also asking MCCY to share how coaches and trainers can be better prepared to coach individuals with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: The Singapore Sports Hall of Fame was set up to recognise and honour outstanding sports personalities who have succeeded in their respective disciplines.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: These sports icons are celebrated for their dedication, determination and passion for excelling and reaching the pinnacle of competitive sports.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: In addition, they serve as beacons of inspiration for current and future generations of athletes in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Many Hall of Famers reached the pinnacle of sports with scarce resources.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Today, our athletes are better funded and resourced, and the expectations have shifted.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: It may be time to consider a revision of admission criteria.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: In addition, Singapore has also produced its fair share of sports administrators and world-class coaches and judges who have contributed globally.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Would MCCY consider including coaches and administrators in the Hall of Fame?

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Can MCCY share its plans for the Sports Hall of Fame and how it intends to activate its inductees?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: The first Hall of Fame ceremony was held in 1999, and by 2003, 50 athletes have been inducted into the Hall of Fame.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: While one could argue that a Hall of Fame inductee must be an exemplary individual, who has not only demonstrated outstanding sporting performance but also a track record of service, imposing eight years is somewhat arbitrary and rather excessive.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: With this criterion, an outstanding athlete, who for whatever reason, is unable to complete eight years of service will not be given the recognition he or she deserves in the Hall of Fame.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Not being able to complete the mandatory eight years of service does not reduce the fact that the athlete has contributed to the local sporting scene, or the international sporting scene, for that matter.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Would MCCY consider a review of the induction criteria given that the last review was almost 20 years ago?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Access to sports for Persons with Disability (PwDs) has always been an important feature in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Back in 1973, several Ministries and eight other organisations came together to jointly found the Singapore Disability Sports Council (SDSC) to encourage PwDs to take up sports as a form of rehabilitative therapy and as a means to realise their potential.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Since then, various initiatives have been implemented to further encourage PwDs’ access to sports and to encourage PwDs to take up sports at a competitive level.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: In 2016, in conjunction with Enabling Masterplan 2, the Disability Sports Masterplan (DSMP) was launched by the Committee of Disability Sports to promote an inclusive society through sports.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: The DSMP had three thrusts: (a) to expand access and opportunities for participation; (b) to develop organisational and professional capabilities and (c) to build awareness and strengthen affinity.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Each of these thrusts, in turn, has specific recommendations that underpin them.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: It has been some years since DSMP has been introduced.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Can MCCY share with us the progress of these initiatives under these thrusts and the take-up rate of the various programmes?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: What are MCCY’s plans to further these initiatives?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Are there gaps that exist in the current programmes and how does the Ministry intend to plug these gaps?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: The sub-committee’s mandate is to explore how to increase participation opportunities in sports amongst students with disabilities in mainstream schools and in special education (SPED) schools.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Can MCCY share perhaps how it has been working with MOE to integrate these programmes into schools, especially mainstream schools, when the needs of students are more diverse?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Chairman, in 2016, the Disability Sports Master Plan (DSMP) was launched to further improve Persons with Disabilities' access to sports.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: PwDs deserve the same level of access to the sports that they wish to pursue as non-PwDs.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: This is regardless of whether the objective is for leisure or to compete at national, regional or international level.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: What is MCCY doing to support and provide more opportunities for aspiring para-athletes, especially for those who wish to pursue sports at a competitive level?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Can MCCY also elaborate on its strategies to provide more inclusive opportunities through sports in the next phase of the Master Plan?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan, you can take both cuts together.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Chairman, we must work at keeping our sports landscape ever more inclusive.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Can the Ministry provide an update on its progress and plans for disability sports as part of the Enabling Master Plan 3.0, both in terms of the uptake and participation in community sports by Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) as well as the growth of and support for high-performance disability sports?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: What are the Ministry's plans to help these professionals refresh and update their skills and build new capabilities?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It helps us keep fit physically and mentally and encourages social interactions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is why sport should continue to be a part of our Singaporean way of life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Hany Soh, Mr Xie Yao Quan and Mr Mark Chay asked about sports facilities that will be constructed and upgraded, as well as plans to make these facilities accessible to Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) and seniors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Easy access to sporting facilities will help us adopt sports as our way of life and we have been pursuing this through the Sports Facilities Master Plan (SFMP).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The master plan is a multi-year effort to refresh infrastructure, increase residents’ accessibility to sports facilities and encourage social mixing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will ensure that our rejuvenated and new facilities cater to seniors and Persons with Disabilities (PwDs).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Residents in Sembawang and Punggol East will also enjoy Sport-in-Precinct (SIP) facilities, with further projects expected to open in Nee Soon Central, Woodlands and Gek Poh in the coming months.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The rejuvenation works at Delta and Choa Chu Kang Sport Centres are also in their final stages.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Both centres are due to open in the first half of this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will also bring more integrated sport and community hubs to residents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: One such example launched last year is Bukit Canberra, which will feature facilities, such as an indoor sports hall, swimming pools, gym, fitness studios, a hawker centre and a polyclinic.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We also launched the roadshow for the Toa Payoh Integrated Development last month.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This would be an exciting lifestyle destination comprising event spaces, sporting facilities, such as a gymnasium, badminton courts, a revamped swimming complex as well as a new library.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Sport Singapore has also been working closely with MOE to expand the Dual-Use Scheme (DUS) to provide Singaporeans with convenient access to schools’ sports facilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To date, these include around 230 school fields and indoor sports halls.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan asked what the Ministry’s plans are to help exercise professionals refresh and update their skills.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Indeed, certified exercise professionals with relevant accreditations play an important role, especially as more Singaporeans adopt sport as a way of life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: From April this year to March next year, we will support our exercise professionals to upskill by providing free membership to the National Instructors and Coaches Association (NICA).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This provides them with access to training support and grants, amongst other benefits.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To register, exercise professionals need to produce the following: (a) Standard First Aid with AED and CPR certification; (b) code of ethics acknowledgment; and (c) relevant fitness or exercise accreditations, such as personal trainer, yoga, zumba or general ones like group fitness instructors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: From April next year, Government agencies which hire a sizeable number of exercise professionals, including Sport Singapore (SportSG), People’s Association (PA), Health Promotion Board (HPB) and Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), will only hire exercise professionals registered under NREP.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This will ensure a certain level and consistency of qualifications amongst all exercise professionals who conduct programmes that are run by Government agencies for the public.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: A later phase will see NREP strengthening the accreditation framework.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Further details of the requirement for a Basic Exercise Science certification and continuous education framework will be released by SportSG in due course.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through NREP, we hope that exercise professionals will be equipped with the relevant accreditations to raise the overall quality and safety standards of the fitness industry.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Mark Chay asked about our plans to ensure that our athletes are well-supported in 2023; a packed year where our athletes will represent Singapore at the Cambodia 2023 SEA Games and ASEAN Para Games, as well as the deferred Hangzhou 2022 Asian and Asian Para Games.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Behind the scenes, our preparations for the Olympic and Paralympic Games in Paris 2024 are also in full swing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Grooming a champion is a multi-year effort and journey that requires holistic support as the athlete progresses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We work closely with the National Sports Associations (NSAs) and design this support on a multi-year basis so that we can continually identify, develop youths and prepare a pipeline of athletes who can excel at the major Games.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With this in mind, we will send around 570 athletes to the 2023 SEA Games.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For many sports, we are sending more athletes than in previous overseas SEA Games.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This speaks to our aspirations to provide more opportunities to our athletes, especially our young ones, to achieve their full potential.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In terms of psychological support, Singapore Sport Institute (SSI) and National Youth Sports Institute (NYSI) proactively monitor our athletes’ mental health.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ahead of major competitions, dedicated teams of sport psychologists and Athlete Life personnel provide one-on-one consults and impart skills to athletes so that they can cope with the mental and emotional issues that they may face.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I call upon all Singaporeans to rally together and give TeamSG athletes our fullest support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Today’s sporting heroes are often legends of tomorrow.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Darryl David and Mr Mark Chay asked whether MCCY intends to review the criteria for athletes to be inducted into the Singapore Sports Hall of Fame and whether MCCY would consider the inclusion of coaches and administrators.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Chairman, the Singapore Sport Hall of Fame was set up in 1985 to honour our top sportsmen and sportswomen, instill a sense of pride among Singaporeans and inspire our budding athletes to emulate the outstanding performances of its inductees.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: However, it is not only strong medal performances that we wish to recognise.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: First, several of our top athletes make sustained contributions to their sport and the community after they retire from active competition.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We appreciate and recognise these contributions on top of their achievements as active athletes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Second, the success of our athletes and the overall development of Singapore sports owe much also to the contributions of sports administrators, coaches and scientists, amongst others.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As Singapore evolves to be an even more inclusive society, sport must continue to play a key role in our community and our way of life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Mark Chay asked how MCCY promotes philanthropy within our sports culture, including through TeamSG Cares that was set up in April last year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through TeamSG Cares, former and present athletes can participate in various giving initiatives or start their own charity or social pursuit for causes close to their hearts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Since the launch of TeamSG Cares, our athletes have been involved in weekly initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These include sport clinics, such as boxing, bowling and football, weekly food distribution activities, school engagements, talks to underprivileged youths and fund-raising activities for the President’s Challenge.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SportSG’s SportCares initiative also uplifts underserved and underprivileged communities, and I would now like to share how the programme has helped this young man, Abdul Thaslim.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: His parents are both blue-collar workers and he has a younger sister with disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Thaslim started out in SportCares in 2013 with the Saturday Night Lights football programme and later moved to the SportCares’ CareRunners Programme when he discovered his passion for running.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Growing up, finances often weighed on Thaslim’s family.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: At one point, Thaslim even contemplated discontinuing his studies so that he can help support the family financially.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With encouragement from his mentors in the SportCares programme, Thaslim pressed on.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: He, subsequently, enrolled into the Youth Coaching Development Programme to fulfil his aspirations of becoming a coach.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Inspired by those who had modelled the values of volunteering to him, Thaslim is now an active youth coach at SportCares and even volunteers with his local Youth Network.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I am extremely proud of Thaslim and wanted to share this story with every one to showcase how sport can actually be a force for good.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui, Mr Darryl David, Mr Mark Chay and Mr Xie Yao Quan asked about efforts to improve accessibility and inclusion in sports and how the Disability Sport Master Plan (DSMP) can spur greater sport participation amongst persons with disabilities (PwDs).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Together with partners such as the Singapore Disability Sports Council (SDSC), Singapore National Paralympic Council (SNPC) and Special Olympics Singapore, SportSG has done so by introducing a whole range of programmes, including learn to-play programmes and the annual Play Inclusive campaign, reaching out to more than 18,000 PwDs to date.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Play Inclusive Campaign, supported by the Ministry of Education (MOE), promotes inclusion through shared sporting experiences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through Play Inclusive, both persons with and without disabilities from the Special Education and mainstream schools train together before participating in unified sports such as goalball.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To better prepare coaches and trainers to coach individuals with disabilities, the DSMP has further developed professional coaching and technical expertise in disability sports.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In partnership with the International Paralympic Committee, SportSG has facilitated training in coaching and technical courses and grown the pool of disability sports coaches in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: CoachSG has incorporated modules on disability sports, such as inclusive coaching practices, in its Community Coaching curriculum.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Today, I would like to talk about this young man again, but this time from a sporting perspective.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Aloysius was introduced to Boccia when he was just seven years old, when his teacher noticed his cognitive abilities and recommended that he take up Boccia as his CCA, even though Primary 1 students typically could not join.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In 2021, Aloysius made his international debut at the Asian Youth Para Games.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Aloysius went up against the top ranked South Korean player – who was actually selected out of a few hundred under-21 players – in the pool stage and lost to him.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But they had a rematch in the finals and Aloysius managed to beat him and grabbed his first gold medal in an international competition.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And that is a 16-year-old we are talking about.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This year, we will hold focus group discussions with partners and stakeholders to harvest more ideas of how we can do so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And I met many of them, both current and retired: Sophie Soon, her brother Colin, Paralympic bronze medallist, Theresa Goh, Darren Chan, Wong Zhi Wei and many proud parents, and family members who were all there, rooting for the para swimmers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But in an ideal world that I envision, there would be many, many more spectating and cheering on our para swimmers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Allies of the disability community, whether or not they have a person with disability in their families or otherwise.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In an ideal world, we should see persons with and without disabilities, enjoying a game of basketball together, able-bodied individuals enjoying goalball with visually impaired players, without curious stares, without the awkward moments of being overly polite.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In fact, in an ideal world, a "para-athlete" should perhaps simply be called an "athlete"!

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: (In Mandarin):   Sports can raise the fitness level of our citizens and bring people from different races, ages, occupations and family backgrounds together as they exercise or participate in sports together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Every Singaporean including people with disabilities (PwDs) can live fulfilling lives through sports.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In the past few years, we have also achieved some success in promoting sports for PwDs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The proportion of sports in which people with and without disabilities participating together has gradually increased, promoting mutual understanding and social inclusion.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: However, there is much more we can do.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Para Sports Academy will continue to cooperate with partners to create more opportunities for PwDs to participate in sports events, develop ways for them to participate in competitive sports to comprehensively showcase their competitive abilities, and nurture more athletes with disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will continue to hold focus group discussions to gather feedback, promote barrier-free environment to support the needs of different PwD groups and provide them with more opportunities to participate in sports.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Last Saturday, I was at the National Para Swimming Championships held at the OCBC Aquatics Centre.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I met many great para swimmers, both current and retired athletes as well as parents and family members who were there to cheer on our para swimmers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Participating in this activity has moved me a lot.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In an ideal world I envision, there would be more spectators cheering on our PwD swimmers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Even though they may not have a PwD in the family, they could still be allies of the PwDs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In an ideal world, we should see people with and without disabilities enjoying sports together without curious stares or awkward moments of being overly polite.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In an ideal world, a para-athlete should simply be called an athlete!

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: (In English): Sir, to conclude, there is a saying that goes "staying active starts with me".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: However, if you allow me to be grammatically incorrect, I would like to say that sport being a Singaporean way of life starts with "I", three "I"s for that matter. "I" for Invigorating – where sport can help us to unwind and stay healthy; "I" for Inspiring – where sport can inspire a nation; and "I" for Inclusive – where sport can truly be a force for good.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: I have a clarification for Minister of State Tan.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: He shared about how our SG Volunteer Centres (VCs) coordinate efforts to match the volunteers and the beneficiaries, and this has grown.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This Digital Kampong will filter volunteer opportunities and better match the needs and interests or preferences of beneficiaries and volunteers, and also provide voluntary welfare organisations, non-profit organisations with the tools to better manage their volunteers, including on medical escorts.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: (In Mandarin)   I thank the Ministers for the replies earlier.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Second, to some arts practitioners, new technologies such as metaverse are rather new concepts.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: How can the Government help them master these new skills and grasp new opportunities?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: How can the Government revitalise and develop our diverse local arts and culture, and empower our arts practitioners and the entire ecosystem?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: (In Mandarin):   Chairman, I would like to thank Ms Tin Pei Ling for her two questions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I agree with her that arts and culture are a valuable asset that can bring people together.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: All of us would remember that during the COVID-19 pandemic, various creative artistic expressions form a positive energy that supports us as we unite to overcome the pandemic.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Building on this foundation, MCCY will partner Singaporeans and arts and cultural practitioners based on the upgraded Our SG Arts Plan and Our SG Heritage Plan 2.0 to shape a more resilient, inclusive and forward looking future.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: MCCY will continue to invest in our arts and cultural practitioners in two ways as they are important in developing our creative economy.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I agree with Ms Tin Pei Ling's two speeches just now.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We hope that arts can be closer to everyday life.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Hence, we will cooperate with different institutions to provide arts practitioners more space for artistic creation, so that arts can be showcased in everyday life.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Preserving our heritage and innovation in arts requires continuous efforts of the individual, society and the Government.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: I have a few clarifications for Minister Tong.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Are the scouted talents then taken out of their current academy or schools and placed into the National Development Centre or would they concurrently train in their current clubs and also the development centre?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: And given that the National Football Development Centre would comprise of youths aged between 13 to 17, will this cannablise the talent for Singapore Sports School and will they be playing in the National School Games (NSGs)?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: If not, will it dilute them, the quality of football in our National School Games?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The intention is for the players to play with their clubs, so if you are with the JSSL, one of the private clubs, or ActiveSG Football Academy (AFA), you continue playing predominantly with the clubs.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In terms of the cannibalisation, the intention is ultimately as I said, to have multiple pathways, so you can stay with the clubs, you can stay with the academies, but you have to converge.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And the best chance of succeeding to build a strong pipeline for the national team is to have this convergence, because we are too small as a country and too small as a pool to have different district pipelines and pools which do not converge.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, the structure and the framework that we have in mind is one where all these clubs and academies converge.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is not just if you play in the SFA that you will be recognised.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If you are in a private club, you could also be scouted and picked up and put into the NDC.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But the idea is to have a full convergence of this into one structure, one framework, one cohesive path and for that team to come together on a regular basis to play.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I also mentioned just now in my speech that this is not something that will be static.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If you make it in one season or one year, it does not mean that you make it in the subsequent years.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: You have got to continually earn your place.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There has to be competitive tension so that you can come in, you can be dropped out from year to year.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: I have one question for Minister of State Low Yen Ling, because she spoke about the arts masterplan.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Can the Minister of State share how our SG Arts Plan for 2023 to 2027, differs from the previous one?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Mr Chairman, I want to thank the Member, Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, for his clarification.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Minister Edwin Tong had earlier briefly outlines some key differences in the next iteration of our SG Plan, the difference between the 2023 vis a vis the 2018.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Very quickly, allow me to elaborate to Members.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We will also work closely with the arts community to help develop competencies needed to tap on all these opportunities, such as IP management skills, thT was briefly touched on by Minister Edwin Tong earlier as well.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The next one, audience centricity, is very important because in the last three years, we have seen how technology really helped the works of our arts and culture scene to travel beyond Singapore.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Other than enjoying a musical performance now, if it is also curated like a production, the audience in other areas in the regional countries and global market can also enjoy it.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: That is why, in the next five years, we will also focus on greater audience centricity, helping our artists and practitioners and arts organisations to reach audiences in a wider scope.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, we will support the arts sector in developing that area, for example, in order to do so, NAC will look at training and capability development for marketing and data analytics, because it is important for us to know our audience and to also know what our audience want to read and enjoy and view.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This can be also organised in collaboration with training providers and industry partners.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: NAC will also cultivate partnerships with other creatives in the adjacent sectors that I talked about earlier, to create new arts experiences in a hybrid form and even through gamification.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Earlier on in my speech, I talked about the beta version of the one-stop portal for us and I hope all the Members and your residents will try this portal when we roll this out.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We will expand possibilities to create and present art through technology.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And again, that is helping our practitioners reach more audiences.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: These include one, art making using digital tools, online art businesses, audience development through the metaverse that I talked about, and place-making.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We will also encourage the use of digital spaces to expand possibilities for presentation and incorporating arts into the everyday lives of Singaporeans so that we can enjoy arts and for arts to remain accessible in our space and precincts where we live, work and play.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: What will be the focus for the disability sports landscape?

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Second, with the upgrading of Toa Payoh Sports Development and Queenstown, are we able to capture some of the heritage that are a part of these precincts in the upgrading of these facilities?

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Third, with respect to the registration of fitness professionals, are private gyms and enterprises also impacted?

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: With respect to this registration, how will SafeSport be part of this?

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: The last point is on Unleash the Roar!

text: It is great to see that some of the coaches will be going away to see some of the best practices.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: So, maybe some of the other sports that will also be part of this going overseas to find best practices.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: But also, as we look outward, we should also look inward.

text: Perhaps some of our best sports or NSAs that have been world beaters, like in table tennis, sailing and aquatics, could also lend its part to Unleash the Roar! and help to share some of these best practices with soccer academies.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Chairman, I thank the Member for his clarifications.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think I will take the first three clarifications that he has made.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: By that, I mean the concept of sport matching.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Disability occurs on a very wide spectrum and across different disability types.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, what you want the person with disability to realise is that there is a sports that suits me, not just in terms of my temperament and also abilities, but also one that suits my condition.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We want to make that concept availed to all persons with disabilities and their caregivers.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: And from there, we can then see how we can look at who are the talents, who is showing promise, and then pick up the next generation of para-athletes from there.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Queenstown is the first satelite HDB town in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: As the local Member of Parliament in Queenstown, when I was having conversations with Sports Singapore, I was also making requests on how we can weave in some of these heritage components into the new make-up of the stadium.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Things like for instance, activities or events that were held in the 1960s and 1970s that were really high point events, that marked what Queenstown really was.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: It was very much a part of Queenstown Swimming Complex in its earlier days.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, I think these will be considered for sure.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, yes, some of the private gyms might be impacted.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: But I think the intent, if you stick to our original mission, it is really to make sure that there is some quality assurance, some basic standards that are being enforced in this industry.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Minister Edwin Tong; I think he wants to respond as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I was going to respond to Mr Mark Chay's last question.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Yes, the intention is to make this available.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Chay, as an ex-professional athlete and also top notch coach, would know that we regularly send our coaches, players, athletes, overseas to gain best practices, learn and to be immersed in an environment at the very highest levels and bring back that learning back to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will have that and we will continue to do that.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Certainly, the learning and thinking behind how we professionalise sport, which is common across all different sports, whether it is in football, aquatics or sailing as you mentioned, we will harness that learning.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: That is why Singapore Sport Institute (SSI) is there, that is why Sport SG is there, to centralise that learning and to deploy as far as possible to other sports so that other sports can also gain from this know-how and the learning.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, all the different strands and pieces that I spoke about earlier in my speech, the scholarship, sending players overseas on foreign scholarships, local scholarships, sports school, centralising the training with the SFAs, the coaching syllabus, pushing everyone through a centralised, cohesive pipeline, which is the NDC, all of these pieces will commence this year.

text: Bearing these questions in mind and also balancing the different needs, we will, of course, welcome the National Day Parade at the Sports Hub.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But we need to think of how best to deploy the asset.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: On the Member's second question, this is again not new.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
